title.zh: 卷二百一十二 列傳第一百三十七 藩鎮盧龍
title.raw: 卷二百一十二 列傳第一百三十七 藩鎮盧龍 Volume 212 Biographies 137: Buffer Region Lulong

sentences.zh: 藩鎮盧龍

translations.literal: Buffer Region Lulong
translations.idiomatic: The Buffer Region of Lulong

sentences.zh: 李懷仙，柳城胡也。

translations.literal: Li Huaixian was a Hu from Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixian was a non-Han tribesman from Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 世事契丹，守營州。

translations.literal: He served the Khitan in affairs and guarded Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served the Khitan and held Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，智數敏給。

translations.literal: He was skilled at mounted archery, and quick and clever in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: An expert horseman and archer, he was sharp-witted and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 祿山之反，以為裨將。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he was made a deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he was appointed a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 史思明盜河南，留次子朝清守幽州，以阿史那玉、高如震輔之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming seized Henan, left his second son Chaocing to guard Youzhou, and had Ashina Yu and Gao Ruzhen assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized control of Henan, he left his second son Chaocing to hold Youzhou, with Ashina Yu and Gao Ruzhen as his aides.

sentences.zh: 朝義殺立，移檄誅朝清。

translations.literal: Chaoyi killed and established himself, and issued a proclamation condemning Chaocing.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoyi killed his father and seized power, he issued a proclamation calling for Chaocing's execution.

sentences.zh: 二將亂，朝義以懷仙為幽州節度使，督兵馳入。

translations.literal: The two generals fell into disorder; Chaoyi made Huaixian military commissioner of Youzhou and drove troops in haste to enter.
translations.idiomatic: With the two generals in disarray, Chaoyi appointed Huaixian military commissioner of Youzhou and sent him racing in with troops.

sentences.zh: 如震欲拒，不及計，乃出迎。

translations.literal: Ruzhen wished to resist but had no time to plan, and so went out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruzhen wanted to resist but could not act in time, and so went out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 懷仙外示寬以安士，居三日，大會，斬如震，州部悉平。

translations.literal: Huaixian outwardly showed leniency to reassure the troops; after three days he held a great assembly, beheaded Ruzhen, and the prefecture and its districts were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixian put on a show of clemency to calm the troops; three days later, at a grand assembly, he executed Ruzhen and brought the prefecture fully under control.

sentences.zh: 朝義敗，將趨范陽。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was defeated and was about to flee toward Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was defeated, he prepared to flee to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 中人駱奉先間遣鐫說，懷仙遂降，使其將李抱忠以兵三千戍范陽。

translations.literal: The eunuch Luo Fengxian secretly sent a messenger to persuade him; Huaixian then surrendered and had his general Li Baozhong garrison Fanyang with three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Luo Fengxian sent a secret envoy to win him over; Huaixian surrendered and posted his general Li Baozhong at Fanyang with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 朝義至，抱忠閉關不內，乃縊死，斬其首，因奉先以獻。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi arrived, Baozhong closed the passes and would not admit him; Chaoyi then hanged himself, his head was cut off, and it was presented through Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi arrived, Baozhong shut the passes against him; Chaoyi hanged himself, and his head was severed and sent to the court through Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩即表懷仙為幽州盧龍節度使，遷檢校兵部尚書，王武威郡。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en immediately memorialized to make Huaixian military commissioner of Youzhou-Lulong, promoted him to acting minister of war, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en promptly recommended Huaixian as military commissioner of Youzhou-Lulong, appointed him acting minister of war, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 屬懷恩反，邊羌挐戰不解，朝廷方勤西師，故懷仙與田承嗣、薛嵩、張忠誌等得招還散亡，治城邑甲兵，自署文武將吏，私貢賦，天子不能制。

translations.literal: Just then Huai'en rebelled, border Qiang fought without cease, and the court was busy with western campaigns; thus Huaixian, along with Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, and Zhang Zhongzhi, was able to gather back scattered fugitives, fortify cities and arm troops, appoint civil and military officers on his own, levy tribute and taxes privately, and the Son of Heaven could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en rebelled and border fighting with the Qiang raged on, the court was absorbed in campaigns to the west; Huaixian, Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others were left free to reassemble scattered forces, rebuild fortifications, appoint their own officials, and collect taxes on their own authority, beyond the emperor's control.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，麾下朱希彩、朱泚、泚弟滔謀殺懷仙，斬閽者以入，希彩不至。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, his subordinates Zhu Xicai, Zhu Ci, and Ci's younger brother Tao plotted to kill Huaixian; they cut down the gatekeepers to enter, but Xicai did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In 768, his subordinates Zhu Xicai, Zhu Ci, and Ci's younger brother Zhu Tao plotted to kill him; they slew the gatekeepers to force entry, but Xicai failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 黎明，泚懼欲亡，滔曰：「謀不成，有死，逃將焉往？」

translations.literal: At dawn Ci feared and wished to flee; Tao said, "If the plot fails, there is death—where would flight take us?"
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Zhu Ci panicked and wanted to flee; Zhu Tao said, "If the plot fails we die anyway—where would running take us?"

sentences.zh: 俄希彩至，共斬懷仙，族其家。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Xicai arrived; together they beheaded Huaixian and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xicai arrived; together they killed Huaixian and wiped out his entire family.

sentences.zh: 希彩自稱留後。

translations.literal: Xicai declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai proclaimed himself acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張忠誌以兵討其亂，不克。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongzhi raised troops to suppress the disorder but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongzhi marched against them but failed to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 代宗因赦罪，詔宰相王縉為節度使，以希彩副之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong therefore pardoned the crime and ordered Grand Counselor Wang Jin as military commissioner, with Xicai as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong granted an amnesty and appointed Grand Counselor Wang Jin military commissioner, with Xicai as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 希彩聞縉至，蒐卒伍，大陳戎備以逆。

translations.literal: When Xicai heard that Jin had arrived, he gathered troops and arrayed military preparations on a grand scale to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xicai learned of Jin's arrival, he mustered his troops and put on a formidable military display to greet him.

sentences.zh: 縉建旌棨徐驅，希彩迎謁恭甚。

translations.literal: Jin raised banners and standards and drove slowly; Xicai came out to meet him with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Jin advanced slowly under his banners and standards; Xicai came out to receive him with elaborate courtesy.

sentences.zh: 縉度不可制，勞軍，閱旬乃還。

translations.literal: Jin judged that he could not control him, rewarded the army, and after ten days returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not bring Xicai to heel, Jin reviewed the troops, and after ten days departed.

sentences.zh: 希彩即領節度。

translations.literal: Xicai then assumed command of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai thereupon took full control of the command.

sentences.zh: 五年，封高密郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 770 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 驁恣不軌，人不堪。

translations.literal: He was arrogant, willful, and lawless, and people could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and unrestrained, he drove his men to the breaking point.

sentences.zh: 七年，其下李瑗間眾之怨，殺之，共推朱泚為留後。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his subordinate Li Yuan, sensing the troops' resentment, killed him, and together they promoted Zhu Ci as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 772 his officer Li Yuan, reading the mood of the discontented troops, killed him, and the army jointly installed Zhu Ci as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 泚自有傳。

translations.literal: Ci has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci has a separate biography elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 朱滔，性變詐多端倪。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao by nature was changeable, deceitful, and full of schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was by nature cunning, treacherous, and endlessly scheming.

sentences.zh: 希彩以同宗倚愛之，使主帳下親兵。

translations.literal: Xicai, because they shared the same clan, relied on and favored him, and had him command the personal troops under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai, who was of the same clan, favored him and put him in charge of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 泚領節度，遣滔將兵三千為天子西乘塞，為諸軍倡。

translations.literal: When Ci took command of the commission, he sent Tao to lead three thousand troops westward to garrison the passes for the Son of Heaven, taking the lead among the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhu Ci assumed command, he sent Zhu Tao west with three thousand men to garrison the frontier passes for the emperor, setting the example for all other forces.

sentences.zh: 始，安、史後，山東雖外臣順，實傲肆不廷。

translations.literal: At first, after An and Shi, although the eastern provinces outwardly submitted as vassals, in truth they were proud, unrestrained, and absent from court.
translations.idiomatic: After the An-Shi rebellion, the eastern provinces paid nominal allegiance to the throne but in practice remained defiant and absent from court.

sentences.zh: 至泚首效款，帝嘉之，召見滔殿中。

translations.literal: When Ci was the first to offer sincere submission, the Emperor praised this and summoned Tao to an audience in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci became the first to submit in earnest, the emperor was pleased and summoned Zhu Tao to an audience in the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「卿材孰與泚多？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked, "Between you and Ci, who has the greater talent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Which of you brothers is the more capable?

sentences.zh: 滔曰：「統禦士眾，方略明辨，臣不及泚；

translations.literal: Tao said, "In commanding troops and in clear strategic judgment, I do not equal Ci;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao replied, "In commanding troops and in strategic judgment, I cannot match Zhu Ci;

sentences.zh: 臣年二十八，獲謁天子，泚長臣五年，未識朝廷，此不及臣。」

translations.literal: I am twenty-eight and have been granted audience with the Son of Heaven; Ci is five years my elder and has not known the court—in this I surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: but I am twenty-eight and have been received at court, whereas Zhu Ci, five years my senior, has never known the capital—in that respect I surpass him."

sentences.zh: 帝愈嘉，特詔勒兵貫王城而出，屯涇州，置酒開遠門餞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was all the more pleased, specially ordered his troops to march through the imperial city, encamped at Jing Prefecture, and set out wine at Kaiyuan Gate to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more impressed. He issued a special order for Zhu Tao's troops to march through the capital, posted them at Jingzhou, and held a farewell banquet at Kaiyuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 戍還，乃謀奪泚兵，詭說曰：「天下諸侯未有朝者，先至，可以得天子意，子孫安矣。」

translations.literal: When he returned from garrison duty, he then plotted to seize Ci's troops, and with deceitful words said, "Among all the feudatories under Heaven, none has yet come to court; whoever arrives first can win the Son of Heaven's favor, and his descendants will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the frontier, he plotted to seize Zhu Ci's army and told him deceitfully, "No regional lord has yet presented himself at court; the first to arrive will win the emperor's favor and secure his line for generations."

sentences.zh: 泚信之，因入朝。

translations.literal: Ci believed him and therefore went to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci believed him and set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 稍不相平，泚遂乞留，西討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Before long they were no longer on good terms; Ci then requested to remain and campaign west against the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Relations between the brothers soon soured; Zhu Ci asked to remain at court and campaign against Tibet in the west.

sentences.zh: 以滔權知留後，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Tao was made acting commissioner and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was appointed acting commissioner and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 滔殺有功者李瑗等二十餘人，威振軍中。

translations.literal: Tao killed more than twenty men of merit including Li Yuan, and his authority shook the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao executed more than twenty distinguished officers including Li Yuan, and his authority over the army was absolute.

sentences.zh: 李惟嶽拒命，滔與成德張孝忠再破之束鹿，取深州，進檢校司徒，遂領節度，賜德、棣二州。

translations.literal: Li Weiyue defied orders; Tao, together with Zhang Xiaozhong of Chengde, again defeated him at Shulu, took Shen Prefecture, was promoted to acting grand marshal, then assumed the commission, and was granted De and Di prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Weiyue defied the court, Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong of Chengde routed him again at Shulu, seized Shen Prefecture, was promoted to acting grand marshal, assumed full command, and received De and Di prefectures as his domain.

sentences.zh: 德宗以康日知為深、趙二州團練使，詔滔還鎮。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong made Kang Rizhi regimental commissioner of Shen and Zhao prefectures and ordered Tao to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong appointed Kang Rizhi regimental commissioner of Shen and Zhao and ordered Zhu Tao back to his post.

sentences.zh: 滔失深州，不平，又請恒、定七州所賦供軍，復不許，愈怨。

translations.literal: Tao had lost Shen Prefecture and was resentful; he also requested the tax revenues of the seven prefectures of Heng and Ding to supply his army, but again was refused, and his resentment grew.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of Shen Prefecture, Zhu Tao was furious; he also petitioned for the tax revenues of seven prefectures in Heng and Ding to supply his army, was refused again, and grew still more bitter.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧圍田悅，悅窮，間滔與王武俊同叛。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui besieged Tian Yue; Yue was desperate, and in the interval Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was then besieging Tian Yue, who was at his wits' end; Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun took the opportunity to rebel together.

sentences.zh: 滔姑子劉怦為涿州刺史，以書諫曰：「司徒身節制，太尉位宰相，恩遇極矣。

translations.literal: Tao's nephew by marriage Liu Ping was prefect of Zhuo Prefecture; he remonstrated by letter, saying, "The Grand Marshal holds a military commission, and the Grand Preceptor holds the rank of grand counselor—the favor shown you could not be greater.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao's nephew by marriage Liu Ping, prefect of Zhuo, wrote to dissuade him: "You hold a military commission and your brother holds the rank of chief minister—the court's favor toward your family could scarcely be greater.

sentences.zh: 今昌平有太尉鄉、司徒裏，不朽業也。

translations.literal: Now in Changping there are the Grand Preceptor's Village and the Grand Marshal's Hamlet—an imperishable achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Changping already has a Grand Preceptor's Village and a Grand Marshal's Hamlet named in your family's honor—that is an achievement that will endure.

sentences.zh: 能以忠順自將，則無不濟。

translations.literal: If you can lead yourself with loyalty and obedience, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If you conduct yourself with loyalty and obedience, nothing need go wrong.

sentences.zh: 比忘上樂戰，不顧成敗如安、史者，今復何有？

translations.literal: Compared with those who forget their superiors and delight in war, heedless of success or failure like An and Shi—what of such men exists now?
translations.idiomatic: Where today are men like An Lushan and Shi Siming, who forgot their sovereign and plunged heedlessly into war regardless of the outcome?

sentences.zh: 司徒圖之，無貽悔。」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, consider this, and do not bring regret upon yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Consider this carefully, Grand Marshal, and do not bring regret upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 滔不從，連兵救悅。

translations.literal: Tao did not follow his advice and joined forces to rescue Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao ignored the warning and marched to Tian Yue's aid.

sentences.zh: 又懼張孝忠之襲，使怦壁險而軍。

translations.literal: He also feared an attack from Zhang Xiaozhong and had Ping encamp in a defensible position with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an attack from Zhang Xiaozhong, he posted Liu Ping with troops in a fortified position.

sentences.zh: 滔激其眾曰：「士蹀血鬥，既下堅城，朝廷乃見奪，奏賞不報。

translations.literal: Tao incited his troops, saying, "Soldiers trampled blood in battle and already took a strong city, yet the court then seized it from us, and our memorials requesting rewards went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao roused his troops, saying, "You fought through blood to capture a fortified city, and the court snatched it away; our petitions for rewards went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 君等疾趨，破馬燧軍以取貲糧，可乎？」

translations.literal: Will you hurry forward, break Ma Sui's army, and seize provisions and grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you march swiftly, smash Ma Sui's army, and seize his supplies?"

sentences.zh: 軍中不應，三號之，乃曰：「幽人死於南者，骸撐不揜，痛藏心髓，奈何復欲暴骨中野乎？

translations.literal: The army did not respond; after three calls they at last said, "Those from You who died in the south—their bones lie uncovered, the pain buried in marrow and heart—why would we again want to expose our bones in the open field?
translations.idiomatic: The troops did not answer. After he shouted three times, they finally replied, "Our men from Youzhou who died in the south still lie unburied—the grief is carved into our bones. Why would we go south again to leave our corpses on some field?

sentences.zh: 司徒兄弟受國寵，士各蒙官賞，願安之，不恤其它。」

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and his brother have received the state's favor; each soldier has received rank and reward—we wish to rest content and care for nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: You and your brother have received the empire's favor; we have all been granted rank and reward. We wish to be left in peace and care for nothing else."

sentences.zh: 滔罷，潛殺不可共亂者數十人。

translations.literal: Tao desisted and secretly killed several dozen who would not join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao gave up and secretly executed several dozen men who refused to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 日知發其謀於燧，天子聞，以悅未下，重起兩寇，即封滔通義郡王，實戶三百。

translations.literal: Rizhi revealed his plot to Sui; when the Son of Heaven heard, because Yue had not yet fallen and two rebels had risen again, he immediately enfeoffed Tao as Prince of Tongyi Commandery with three hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Rizhi exposed the plot to Ma Sui; learning that Tian Yue still held out and two new rebels had risen, the emperor promptly enfeoffed Zhu Tao as Prince of Tongyi with three hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 滔愈悖，分兵與武俊屯趙州脅日知，矯詔發其糧貯，即引兵救悅，次束鹿。

translations.literal: Tao grew all the more rebellious; he divided troops with Wujun to encamp at Zhao Prefecture and intimidate Rizhi, forged an edict to seize his grain stores, then led troops to rescue Yue and halted at Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao grew bolder still. He split forces with Wang Wujun to threaten Kang Rizhi at Zhao Prefecture, forged an edict to seize his grain stores, then marched to relieve Tian Yue and halted at Shulu.

sentences.zh: 軍大噪曰：「天子令司徒北還，而南救魏，寧有詔邪？」

translations.literal: The army raised a great clamor, saying, "The Son of Heaven ordered the Grand Marshal to return north, yet he goes south to save Wei—is there really such an edict?"
translations.idiomatic: The troops erupted in uproar: "The emperor ordered the Grand Marshal to return north—what edict sends him south to save Wei?"

sentences.zh: 滔懼，走匿傳舍。

translations.literal: Tao was afraid and fled to hide in a relay station.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao panicked and hid in a relay station.

sentences.zh: 裨將蔡雄好諭士曰：「始天子約取成德，所得州縣賜有功者。

translations.literal: Deputy general Cai Xionghao addressed the troops, saying, "At the outset the Son of Heaven agreed that when Chengde was taken, the prefectures and counties obtained would be granted to those with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Cai Xionghao reasoned with the men: "The emperor promised that when Chengde was taken, captured prefectures would go to those who earned them.

sentences.zh: 拔深州者，燕也。

translations.literal: Those who captured Shen Prefecture were the men of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: It was our Yan troops who took Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本鎮常苦無絲纊，冀得深州以佐調率，今顧不得。

translations.literal: Our command has long suffered from lack of silk and cotton; we hoped to gain Shen Prefecture to help meet levies, yet now we cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Our command has always lacked silk and cotton; we counted on Shen Prefecture to help meet our tax quotas, and now it has been taken from us.

sentences.zh: 又天子以帛賜有功士，為馬燧掠去，今引而南，非自為也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven granted silk to reward meritorious soldiers, but it was seized by Ma Sui; now we march south—not for our own sake."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the silk the emperor granted our meritorious soldiers was seized by Ma Sui; we march south now not of our own choosing."

sentences.zh: 軍中悔謝，復曰：「雖然，司徒南行違詔書，莫如還。」

translations.literal: The army repented and apologized, then said again, "Even so, the Grand Marshal's march south violates the edict—it would be better to return."
translations.idiomatic: The troops relented and apologized, then added, "Even so, marching south defies the emperor's order. We had better turn back."

sentences.zh: 滔回次深州，誅首變者二百人。

translations.literal: Tao turned back and halted at Shen Prefecture, executing two hundred ringleaders of the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao turned back and halted at Shen Prefecture, executing two hundred ringleaders of the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，乃率兵南壁寧晉，與武俊合。

translations.literal: The troops were afraid; he then led the army south to fortify at Ningjin and joined with Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were terrified; he then marched south, fortified at Ningjin, and joined Wang Wujun.

sentences.zh: 帝命馬燧、李懷光擊之，滔屬鄭雲逵、田景仙皆奔燧。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Ma Sui and Li Huai'guang to attack him; Tao's subordinates Zheng Yunkui and Tian Jingxian both fled to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ma Sui and Li Huai'guang to attack him; Zhu Tao's officers Zheng Yunkui and Tian Jingxian both defected to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 已而滔破懷光軍，則與王師屯魏橋，久不戰。

translations.literal: Before long Tao defeated Huai'guang's army, then encamped with the royal forces at Weiqiao, and for a long time there was no battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao soon routed Li Huai'guang's army, then faced the imperial forces at Weiqiao, where both sides remained locked in stalemate for a long time.

sentences.zh: 悅德滔援，欲尊而臣之，滔讓武俊，曰：「篋山之勝，王大夫力也。」

translations.literal: Yue was grateful for Tao's aid and wished to honor him as lord and serve as his subject; Tao yielded to Wujun, saying, "The victory at Qieshan was the effort of Grand Master Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Zhu Tao's aid, Tian Yue wished to honor him as overlord and submit as his vassal; Zhu Tao deferred to Wang Wujun, saying, "The victory at Qieshan was Wang's achievement."

sentences.zh: 於是，滔、武俊官屬共議：「古有列國連衡共抗秦。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials of Tao and Wujun jointly deliberated: "In antiquity the feudal states joined in horizontal alliance to resist Qin together.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's and Wang Wujun's staffs then deliberated together: "In antiquity the warring states formed horizontal alliances to resist Qin.

sentences.zh: 今公等在此，李大夫在鄆，請如七國，並建號，用天子正朔。

translations.literal: Now you lords are here, and Grand Master Li is at Yun—let us, like the Seven States, all establish titles and use the Son of Heaven's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: You lords are here and Grand Master Li is at Yun; let us, like the Seven Warring States, each proclaim a royal title while still using the emperor's calendar.

sentences.zh: 且師在外，其動無名，豈長為叛臣，士何所歸？

translations.literal: Moreover, with armies abroad, their movements have no proper name—how can they long remain rebel ministers? Where would the soldiers find their place?
translations.idiomatic: With armies in the field, our cause lacks a proper name; how long can we remain mere rebels? Where would our soldiers find their loyalty?

sentences.zh: 宜擇日定約，順人心，不如盟者共伐之。」

translations.literal: We should choose a day to fix the covenant, follow the people's hearts, and jointly attack any who will not join the alliance."
translations.idiomatic: Let us choose a day to seal an alliance, win the hearts of our men, and jointly attack any who refuse to join."

sentences.zh: 滔等從之。

translations.literal: Tao and the others followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 滔以祿山、思明皆起燕，俄覆滅，惡其名，以冀堯所都，因號冀，武俊號趙，悅號魏，納號齊。

translations.literal: Tao, because Lushan and Siming both rose from Yan and soon perished, disliked that name; because Ji was where Yao had his capital, he therefore took the title Ji; Wujun took Zhao, Yue took Wei, and Na took Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, noting that both An Lushan and Shi Siming had risen from Yan only to be swiftly destroyed, shunned that name; because Ji had been Yao's capital, he styled himself King of Ji; Wang Wujun took Zhao, Tian Yue took Wei, and Li Na took Qi.

sentences.zh: 建中三年冬十月庚申，為壇魏西，祀天，各僭為王，與武俊等三讓乃就位。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the tenth month of winter in the third year of Jianzhong, they built an altar west of Wei, sacrificed to Heaven, each usurped the title of king, and with Wujun and the others performed three declinations before taking their seats.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the tenth month of 782, they built an altar west of Wei, sacrificed to Heaven, each proclaimed himself king, and after three ceremonial refusals with Wang Wujun and the others took their thrones.

sentences.zh: 滔為盟主，稱孤；

translations.literal: Tao was leader of the alliance and called himself Gu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, as leader of the alliance, styled himself Gu;

sentences.zh: 武俊、悅及納稱寡人。

translations.literal: Wujun, Yue, and Na called themselves Guaren.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na styled themselves Guaren.

sentences.zh: 是日，三叛軍上有雲氣頗異，燧望笑曰：「是雲無知，乃為賊瑞邪！」

translations.literal: That day, above the three rebel armies there was a cloud formation quite unusual; Sui looked up and laughed, saying, "This cloud knows nothing—could it really be an auspicious sign for bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: That day an unusual cloud formation appeared above the three rebel armies; Ma Sui looked up and laughed, "That cloud knows nothing—does it think it brings good fortune to rebels?"

sentences.zh: 先是，其地土息高三丈，魏人韋稔佞悅，以為益土之兆。

translations.literal: Earlier, at that place a mound of earth had risen three zhang high; Wei native Wei Ren, flattering Yue, took it as an omen of increased territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a mound of earth three zhang high had risen at that spot; Wei Ren, a native of Wei who flattered Tian Yue, had taken it as an omen of territorial expansion.

sentences.zh: 後二年，滔等冊壝，正值其所。

translations.literal: Two years later, when Tao and the others raised the altar mound, it happened to be exactly at that spot.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when Zhu Tao and the others built their sacrificial mound, it stood precisely on that spot.

sentences.zh: 滔改幽州為范陽府，以子為府留後，稱元帥，用親信為留守。

translations.literal: Tao changed Youzhou to Fanyang Prefecture, made his son acting prefect of the prefecture, styled himself commander-in-chief, and appointed trusted men as resident commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao renamed Youzhou Fanyang Prefecture, appointed his son acting prefect, styled himself commander-in-chief, and posted trusted men as resident commissioners.

sentences.zh: 滔等居室皆曰殿，妻曰妃，子為國公，下皆稱臣，謂殿下。

translations.literal: Tao and the others called their residences palaces, their wives consorts, their sons state dukes; subordinates all called themselves ministers and addressed them as Dianxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and the others called their residences palaces, their wives consorts, their sons state dukes; subordinates styled themselves ministers and addressed them as Dianxia.

sentences.zh: 上書曰箋，所下曰令。

translations.literal: Documents submitted upward were called jian; those issued downward were called ling.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions to superiors were styled jian; orders issued downward were styled ling.

sentences.zh: 置左右內史，視丞相；

translations.literal: He established Left and Right Inner Scribes, equivalent to chief counselors;
translations.idiomatic: He established Left and Right Inner Scribes, equivalent to chief counselors;

sentences.zh: 內史令、監，視侍中、中書令；

translations.literal: Inner Scribe Directors and Supervisors, equivalent to attendants-in-chief and heads of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Inner Scribe Directors and Supervisors, equivalent to attendants-in-chief and heads of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 東西侍郎，視門下、中書；

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Vice Ministers, equivalent to the Chancellery and Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Vice Ministers, equivalent to the Chancellery and Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 東曹給事、西曹舍人，視給事中、中書舍人；

translations.literal: Eastern Bureau Attendants and Western Bureau Drafting Officers, equivalent to supervising secretaries and drafting officers of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Bureau Attendants and Western Bureau Drafting Officers, equivalent to supervising secretaries and drafting officers of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 司議大夫，視諫議大夫；

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grand Masters, equivalent to remonstrance grand masters;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandees, equivalent to remonstrance grandees;

sentences.zh: 六官省，視尚書；

translations.literal: Six Bureaus Department, equivalent to the Ministry of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Six Bureaus Department, equivalent to the Ministry of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 東、西曹僕射，視左右僕射；

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Bureau Vice Directors, equivalent to Left and Right Vice Directors;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Bureau Vice Directors, equivalent to Left and Right Vice Directors;

sentences.zh: 御史臺曰執憲，置大夫至監察御史，驅使要籍官曰承令；

translations.literal: The Censorate was called Execution of Law; grand censors down to investigating censors were appointed; attendants on the registry who carried orders were called Order Bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was renamed Execution of Law, with grand censors down to investigating censors; attendants on the registry who carried orders were styled Order Bearers;

sentences.zh: 左右將軍曰虎牙、豹略；

translations.literal: Left and Right Generals were called Tiger Fang and Leopard Strategy;
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Generals were styled Tiger Fang and Leopard Strategy;

sentences.zh: 軍使曰鷹揚、龍驤。

translations.literal: Army commissioners were called Soaring Hawk and Dragon Charger.
translations.idiomatic: Army commissioners were styled Soaring Hawk and Dragon Charger.

sentences.zh: 以劉怦為范陽府留守，柳良器、李子千為左右內史，滔兄瓊瑰、陸慶為東、西曹仆射，楊霽、馬寔、寇瞻、楊榮國為司文、司武、司禮、司刑侍郎，李士真、樊播為執憲大夫、中丞。

translations.literal: He made Liu Ping resident commissioner of Fanyang Prefecture; Liu Liangqi and Li Ziqian Left and Right Inner Scribes; Tao's elder brother Qionghui and Lu Qing Eastern and Western Bureau Vice Directors; Yang Ji, Ma Shi, Kou Zhan, and Yang Rongguo Vice Ministers of Documents, War, Rites, and Punishments; and Li Shizhen and Fan Bo grand censor and vice censor of Execution of Law.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Ping resident commissioner of Fanyang Prefecture; Liu Liangqi and Li Ziqian as Left and Right Inner Scribes; Zhu Tao's elder brother Qionghui and Lu Qing as Eastern and Western Bureau Vice Directors; Yang Ji, Ma Shi, Kou Zhan, and Yang Rongguo as Vice Ministers of Documents, War, Rites, and Punishments; and Li Shizhen and Fan Bo as grand censor and vice censor of Execution of Law.

sentences.zh: 其餘以次補署。

translations.literal: The rest were appointed in order according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: All remaining posts were filled in order of precedence.

sentences.zh: 聘處士張遂、王道為司諫。

translations.literal: He engaged the recluses Zhang Sui and Wang Dao as remonstrance officers.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited the recluses Zhang Sui and Wang Dao as remonstrance officers.

sentences.zh: 燧遣李晟將兵至易、定，率張茂昭攻涿、莫，以絕滔援。

translations.literal: Sui sent Li Sheng to lead troops to Yi and Ding, and had Zhang Maozhao attack Zhuo and Mo to cut off Tao's reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui dispatched Li Sheng with troops to Yi and Ding and had Zhang Maozhao attack Zhuo and Mo to sever Zhu Tao's line of supply.

sentences.zh: 明年，圍清苑，滔將鄭景濟固守。

translations.literal: The next year they besieged Qingyuan; Tao's general Zheng Jingji held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they besieged Qingyuan, where Zhu Tao's general Zheng Jingji held the defenses.

sentences.zh: 滔使馬寔將兵萬人，與武俊拒燧，自以兵萬餘救清苑，絕晟糧道。

translations.literal: Tao sent Ma Shi to lead ten thousand troops with Wujun to resist Sui, and himself led more than ten thousand to relieve Qingyuan and cut off Sheng's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao sent Ma Shi with ten thousand men to join Wang Wujun against Ma Sui, while he personally led more than ten thousand to relieve Qingyuan and cut Li Sheng's supply line.

sentences.zh: 兵至定州，晟不知，夜引兵還。

translations.literal: When the troops reached Ding Prefecture, Sheng did not know and withdrew his army by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao's army reached Ding Prefecture, Li Sheng was unaware and withdrew his forces under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 滔疑有伏，不敢逼，遽保瀛州。

translations.literal: Tao suspected an ambush, dared not press close, and hastily secured Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao suspected an ambush, dared not press the pursuit, and hastily fell back to Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而孝忠、晟合兵千人城萊水，滔驍將烏薩戒以兵七百襲殺城卒數百，晟不出。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xiaozhong and Sheng combined a thousand troops to fortify Laishui; Tao's fierce general Wusa Jie with seven hundred men made a surprise attack and killed several hundred garrison soldiers, but Sheng did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Xiaozhong and Li Sheng combined a thousand men to fortify Laishui; Zhu Tao's fierce general Wusa Jie raided with seven hundred troops and killed several hundred garrison soldiers, but Li Sheng would not sally out.

sentences.zh: 景濟望滔軍立幟為應。

translations.literal: Jingji looked toward Tao's army and raised banners in response.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jingji watched for Zhu Tao's army and raised banners in signal.

sentences.zh: 滔進軍薄晟營，晟戰不利，城中兵亦出，晟大敗，奔易州。

translations.literal: Tao advanced and pressed close to Sheng's camp; Sheng fought unfavorably, troops from the city also came out, Sheng was greatly defeated and fled to Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao pressed Li Sheng's camp; Li Sheng fought poorly, the city's garrison sallied forth, and he was routed and fled to Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 茂昭走滿城。

translations.literal: Maozhao fled to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao retreated to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 滔已破晟，則回屯河間不進。

translations.literal: Tao having already defeated Sheng, then encamped at Hejian and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Having defeated Li Sheng, Zhu Tao encamped at Hejian and made no further advance.

sentences.zh: 武俊使宋端趣讓，滔怒曰：「孤亟戰且病，就醫藥，而王已復云云。

translations.literal: Wujun sent Song Duan to urge and reproach him; Tao angrily said, "Gu has fought repeatedly and is ill, seeking medicine, yet the King again speaks thus.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun sent Song Duan to press and reproach him; Zhu Tao fumed, "I have fought repeatedly and am ill, seeking medicine, yet the King speaks thus again.

sentences.zh: 孤南救魏，棄兄背君如脫屣。

translations.literal: Gu went south to save Wei, abandoning my elder brother and betraying my sovereign as easily as casting off shoes.
translations.idiomatic: I marched south to save Wei, abandoning my brother and betraying the emperor as easily as casting off shoes.

sentences.zh: 王必相疑，亦聽所為！」

translations.literal: The King must surely suspect me—let him do as he pleases!"
translations.idiomatic: The King must surely distrust me—let him do as he will!"

sentences.zh: 端還，武俊謂寔曰：「寡人望王速來指縱，決勝負，復何惡？

translations.literal: When Duan returned, Wujun said to Shi, "Guaren hoped the King would come quickly to direct operations and decide victory or defeat—what offense is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: When Song Duan returned, Wang Wujun told Ma Shi, "I only wanted the King to come quickly to direct operations and settle the outcome—what offense is there in that?

sentences.zh: 王異日並天下，寡人得六七城，為節度足矣。」

translations.literal: When the King one day unites the realm, if Guaren obtains six or seven cities and holds a military commission, that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: When the King one day unites the realm, six or seven cities and a military commission will be enough for me."

sentences.zh: 寔遣具道所以然，武俊亦遣使謝滔，滔悅，亦報謝。

translations.literal: Shi sent a messenger to explain the reason in full; Wujun also sent an envoy to apologize to Tao, and Tao was pleased and sent thanks in return.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi sent a full explanation; Wang Wujun also dispatched an envoy to apologize to Zhu Tao, who was mollified and returned thanks.

sentences.zh: 然武俊內銜之，滋不懌，與田悅潛謀絕滔。

translations.literal: Yet Wujun harbored resentment inwardly and grew increasingly displeased; with Tian Yue he secretly plotted to cut off Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Wujun nursed a grudge and grew ever more discontented; with Tian Yue he secretly plotted to break with Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 及泚反，燧等皆班師，武俊、寔亦還。

translations.literal: When Ci rebelled, Sui and the others all withdrew their armies; Wujun and Shi also returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Ma Sui and the others withdrew their armies; Wang Wujun and Ma Shi also returned.

sentences.zh: 悅、武俊遣使至河間，賀泚即位。

translations.literal: Yue and Wujun sent envoys to Hejian to congratulate Ci on his accession.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue and Wang Wujun sent envoys to Hejian to congratulate Zhu Ci on his accession.

sentences.zh: 武俊詭請寔共攻康日知於趙州，謀覆其軍，不克。

translations.literal: Wujun deceitfully asked Shi to join in attacking Kang Rizhi at Zhao Prefecture, plotting to destroy his army, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun falsely invited Ma Shi to join an attack on Kang Rizhi at Zhao Prefecture, intending to destroy his army, but failed.

sentences.zh: 實歸，武俊餞之，厚贈遺。

translations.literal: When Shi returned, Wujun gave him a farewell feast and sent rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Shi returned, Wang Wujun entertained him at a farewell feast and sent lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 泚遣人密召滔，使趨洛陽。

translations.literal: Ci secretly summoned Tao and had him hurry to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci secretly summoned Zhu Tao and ordered him to march on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 滔發書，西向再拜，移檄諸道曰：「今發突騎四十萬走洛陽，與皇帝會上陽宮。」

translations.literal: Tao issued a letter, bowed twice toward the west, and circulated a proclamation to all circuits, saying, "Now I dispatch four hundred thousand mounted shock troops racing to Luoyang to meet the Emperor at Shangyang Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao issued a proclamation, bowed twice toward the west, and circulated it to all circuits: "I now dispatch four hundred thousand mounted shock troops racing to Luoyang to meet the emperor at Shangyang Palace."

sentences.zh: 使王郅說悅連和俱西。

translations.literal: He had Wang Zhi persuade Yue to join in alliance and march west together.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhi to persuade Tian Yue to join the alliance and march west together.

sentences.zh: 滔素強調斂，武俊等不能堪。

translations.literal: Tao had always imposed heavy levies, and Wujun and the others could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao had always imposed heavy levies, which Wang Wujun and the others could scarcely bear.

sentences.zh: 又令各以兵五千從攻洛，欲僭稱帝，乘輿、法從及赦令皆具。

translations.literal: He also ordered each to bring five thousand troops to join the attack on Luoyang; he wished to usurp the title of emperor, and the imperial carriage, ceremonial retinue, and amnesty edicts were all prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered each ally to contribute five thousand troops for the assault on Luoyang; he planned to usurp the imperial title, and had already prepared an imperial carriage, ceremonial retinue, and amnesty edicts.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇以女妻奚王，大歷末，奚亂，殺王，女逃歸，道平盧，滔以錦繡張道，待其至，請為婚，女悅，許焉。

translations.literal: At first the Uyghurs gave a daughter in marriage to the Xi king; at the end of Dali the Xi rebelled, killed the king, and the daughter fled back; passing through Pinglu, Tao spread brocades and silks along the road, waited for her arrival, and requested marriage; the daughter was pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Uyghurs had given a princess to the Xi king; when the Xi rebelled at the end of the Dali era and killed their king, the princess fled homeward. Passing through Pinglu, Zhu Tao spread brocades and silks along the road, received her, and proposed marriage; she accepted.

sentences.zh: 既而遣使修婿禮於回紇，回紇喜，報以名馬重寶。

translations.literal: Thereafter he sent envoys to perform marriage rites with the Uyghurs; the Uyghurs were pleased and responded with famous horses and precious goods.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to complete the marriage rites with the Uyghurs, who responded with famed horses and precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 及僭相王，與武俊、悅、納納四金鑰於回紇，曰：「四國願聽命於可汗，謹上金鑰，啟閉出納，唯所命。」

translations.literal: When they usurped mutual kingship, together with Wujun, Yue, and Na they presented four golden keys to the Uyghurs, saying, "The four states wish to obey the Qaghan's commands; we respectfully present golden keys—opening, closing, disbursement, and receipt are all at your command."
translations.idiomatic: When they proclaimed themselves kings, Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na presented four golden keys to the Uyghurs, saying, "Our four states submit to the Qaghan's command; we respectfully offer these golden keys—opening, closing, disbursement, and receipt are all at your will."

sentences.zh: 至是，乞師焉。

translations.literal: At this time they requested military aid.
translations.idiomatic: Now they requested Uyghur troops.

sentences.zh: 回紇以二千騎從，而武俊亦先乞師，以斷懷光餉路，未至，而王師還。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs followed with two thousand horsemen; Wujun had also earlier requested troops to cut Huai'guang's supply route, but before they arrived the royal army had returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs followed with two thousand horsemen; Wang Wujun had also requested troops to cut Li Huai'guang's supply line, but before they arrived the imperial army had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 回紇過幽州，滔使說其酋達幹曰：「若能同度河而南，玉帛子女不貲，計可得也。」

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs passed through Youzhou, Tao sent someone to persuade their chieftain Tagan, saying, "If you can cross the river south together, silks, goods, women, and children beyond counting can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: As the Uyghurs passed through Youzhou, Zhu Tao sent an envoy to persuade their chieftain Tagan: "If you cross the river south with us, silks, goods, women, and children beyond counting await you."

sentences.zh: 達幹許諾，滔啖以金帛，約曰：「五十里舍，以須悅軍。」

translations.literal: Tagan agreed; Tao tempted him with gold and silks and agreed, saying, "Camp every fifty li and wait for Yue's army."
translations.idiomatic: Tagan agreed; Zhu Tao bribed him with gold and silks and stipulated, "Camp every fifty li and wait for Tian Yue's army."

sentences.zh: 滔兵五萬，車千乘，騎二萬，士私屬萬餘，虜兵三千，馬、橐它倍之；

translations.literal: Tao's troops numbered fifty thousand, with a thousand chariots, twenty thousand horsemen, more than ten thousand personal followers of soldiers, three thousand barbarian troops, and horses and camels twice that number;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao marched with fifty thousand troops, a thousand chariots, twenty thousand cavalry, more than ten thousand soldiers' personal followers, three thousand allied barbarian troops, and twice as many horses and camels;

sentences.zh: 過武俊境，武俊勞之，牛酒芻米皆具。

translations.literal: passing through Wujun's territory, Wujun entertained them, providing cattle, wine, fodder, and grain in full.
translations.idiomatic: passing through Wang Wujun's territory, where Wang Wujun entertained them with cattle, wine, fodder, and grain in abundance.

sentences.zh: 然悅已用武俊謀，不肯出，儲峙於野以待。

translations.literal: Yet Yue had already adopted Wujun's plan and refused to come out, storing supplies in the open country to wait.
translations.idiomatic: But Tian Yue, following Wang Wujun's counsel, refused to march out and instead stockpiled supplies in the open country to wait.

sentences.zh: 滔至貝州，悅刺史邢曹俊上謁滔，即歸閉城守，滔疑之，次永濟。

translations.literal: When Tao reached Bei Prefecture, Yue's prefect Xing Caojun came up to pay respects to Tao, then returned and closed the city in defense; Tao was suspicious and halted at Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao reached Bei Prefecture, Tian Yue's prefect Xing Caojun paid his respects then returned to shut the city gates; Zhu Tao grew suspicious and halted at Yongji.

sentences.zh: 武俊陰遣客反間滔曰：「悅有憾，須公南，以兵斷公歸路，宜少備。」

translations.literal: Wujun secretly sent an agent with counter-intelligence to Tao, saying, "Yue bears a grudge; once you go south he will use troops to cut your return route—you should take some precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun secretly sent an agent to sow discord, telling Zhu Tao, "Tian Yue bears a grudge; once you march south he will cut your retreat—you should take precautions."

sentences.zh: 滔聞怒，入永濟，執悅吏掠訊，不得其情，殺之。

translations.literal: When Tao heard this he was enraged; entering Yongji he seized Yue's officials and tortured them for interrogation, could not obtain the truth, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao flew into a rage, entered Yongji, seized Tian Yue's officials and tortured them for information, learned nothing, and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 使回紇大掠，南及澶、衛，系執老幼無遺者。

translations.literal: He had the Uyghurs plunder on a grand scale, south as far as Chan and Wei, seizing old and young without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He unleashed the Uyghurs to plunder south as far as Chan and Wei, seizing every man, woman, and child they could find.

sentences.zh: 悅大恐，闔城自保。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly afraid and shut the entire city to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was terrified and shut himself inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 滔遣將楊布略定館陶，屯平恩，置官吏。

translations.literal: Tao sent his general Yang Bu to pacify Guantao, encamped at Ping'en, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao sent his general Yang Bu to pacify Guantao, posted troops at Ping'en, and installed local officials.

sentences.zh: 滔整軍北還，使馬寔屯冠氏，聞悅死，遂攻魏州，圍貝州。

translations.literal: Tao reorganized his army and returned north, had Ma Shi encamp at Guanshi; hearing that Yue had died, he then attacked Wei Prefecture and besieged Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao reorganized his army and marched north, posting Ma Shi at Guanshi; on hearing of Tian Yue's death he attacked Wei Prefecture and besieged Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是，武俊、李抱真合軍擊滔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wujun and Li Baozhen combined armies to attack Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun and Li Baozhen then joined forces to attack Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔急召寔至貝州，步馬乏頓。

translations.literal: Tao urgently summoned Shi to Bei Prefecture; infantry and cavalry were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao urgently recalled Ma Shi to Bei Prefecture; his infantry and cavalry were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 明日，輒約戰，寔請休士三日，蔡雄、達幹等畏武俊堅壁難圖，請戰。

translations.literal: The next day he immediately offered battle; Shi requested three days' rest for the troops; Cai Xiong, Tagan, and others feared Wujun's fortified walls would be hard to overcome and urged battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhu Tao offered battle at once; Ma Shi asked for three days' rest for the troops; Cai Xiong, Tagan, and others, fearing Wang Wujun's fortified position would be hard to crack, urged him to fight.

sentences.zh: 楊布曰：「大王將取東都，逢小敵即怯，何以長驅天下邪？」

translations.literal: Yang Bu said, "Great King intends to take the Eastern Capital—if you flinch before a small enemy, how can you drive far across the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bu said, "Your Majesty intends to take the Eastern Capital—if you flinch before a minor foe, how can you sweep across the realm?"

sentences.zh: 術士尹少伯亦言必勝。

translations.literal: The diviner Yin Shaobo also said victory was certain.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Yin Shaobo also declared certain victory.

sentences.zh: 既戰，為二軍所乘，大敗，大將朱良祐、李進皆被執，委杖如丘，滔奔入德州。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, he was taken advantage of by the two armies and suffered great defeat; great generals Zhu Liangyou and Li Jin were both captured, abandoned weapons piled like hills, and Tao fled into De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, the two armies seized their advantage and routed him; his great generals Zhu Liangyou and Li Jin were captured, abandoned weapons piled like hills, and Zhu Tao fled into De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 恨少伯、雄、布之謬，殺之。

translations.literal: He resented the errors of Shaobo, Xiong, and Bu and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming Shaobo, Xiong, and Bu for their bad counsel, he had them executed.

sentences.zh: 俄而京師平，滔已敗，不能軍，走還幽州，上書待罪。

translations.literal: Before long the capital was pacified; Tao had already been defeated and could not maintain his army; he fled back to Youzhou and submitted a letter awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the capital was restored; Zhu Tao, already defeated and unable to hold his army together, fled back to Youzhou and submitted a letter awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 有詔武俊、抱真開示大信，若誠心審固者，當洗釁錄勛，與更始。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wujun and Baozhen to proclaim great good faith: if sincerity was truly firm, their offenses would be washed away, merit recorded, and they would be given a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed Wang Wujun and Li Baozhen to offer full amnesty: those who proved sincerely loyal would have their offenses wiped clean, their merit recorded, and be given a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 劉怦，幽州昌平人。

translations.literal: Liu Ping was a native of Changping in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping was a native of Changping in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為范陽裨將，以親老疾宜侍，輒去職。

translations.literal: In youth he was a deputy general at Fanyang; because his parents were old and ill and needed care, he repeatedly left his post.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as a deputy general at Fanyang; when his parents grew old and ill he repeatedly resigned to care for them.

sentences.zh: 李懷仙為節度使，檄召不應。

translations.literal: When Li Huaixian was military commissioner, he issued summonses but Ping did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaixian was military commissioner, he issued summonses, but Liu Ping did not respond.

sentences.zh: 朱滔時，積功至雄武軍使，廣墾田，節用度，以辦治稱。

translations.literal: Under Zhu Tao he accumulated merit until he became commissioner of the Xiongwu Army; he expanded reclaimed fields, economized expenditures, and was known for efficient administration.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhu Tao he rose through merit to commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, expanding reclaimed farmland, economizing expenditures, and earning a reputation for efficient administration.

sentences.zh: 稍遷涿州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to prefect of Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 滔之討田承嗣，表知府事，和裕得眾心。

translations.literal: When Tao campaigned against Tian Chengsi, he memorialized to have Ping manage prefectural affairs; Ping was gentle and generous and won the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao campaigned against Tian Chengsi, he appointed Liu Ping to manage prefectural affairs; gentle and generous, he won the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李寶臣以兵劫滔於瓦橋，滔走，寶臣乘勝欲襲幽州，怦設方略，勒兵完守，寶臣不敢謀，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: Li Baochen with troops waylaid Tao at Waqiao; Tao fled, and Baochen, pressing his victory, wished to strike Youzhou; Ping devised strategy, mustered troops and completed the defenses, and Baochen dared not plot further; Ping was promoted to vice censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen ambushed Zhu Tao at Waqiao; Zhu Tao fled, and Baochen, pressing his advantage, planned to strike Youzhou; Liu Ping devised defenses, mustered troops, and completed the fortifications, and Baochen dared not attack; Liu Ping was promoted to vice censor.

sentences.zh: 滔敗歸，終不貳，益治兵，人嘉怦忠於所奉。

translations.literal: When Tao returned defeated, Ping never wavered in loyalty, further trained troops, and people praised Ping's fidelity to those he served.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao returned defeated, Liu Ping never wavered in loyalty, redoubled his military preparations, and people praised his fidelity to his lord.

sentences.zh: 及滔死，軍中盡推怦，乃總軍事。

translations.literal: When Tao died, the entire army promoted Ping, and he then assumed overall military command.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao died, the army unanimously supported Liu Ping, who assumed overall command.

sentences.zh: 俄詔為節度副大使、彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to be deputy military commissioner and Duke of Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed deputy military commissioner and Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 居鎮才三月死，年五十九，贈兵部尚書，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He had held the command only three months when he died, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously granted minister of war and given the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He had held command only three months when he died at fifty-nine; he was posthumously appointed minister of war and given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子濟。

translations.literal: His son was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 濟，字濟。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, courtesy name Ji.

sentences.zh: 遊學京師，第進士，歷莫州刺史。

translations.literal: He studied in the capital, passed the jinshi examination, and served as prefect of Mo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in the capital, passed the jinshi examination, and served as prefect of Mo.

sentences.zh: 怦病，詔濟假州事。

translations.literal: When Ping fell ill, an edict had Ji act in prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ping fell ill, an edict appointed Liu Ji acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 及怦卒，嗣節度，累遷檢校尚書右仆射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Ping died, Ji succeeded to the military commission and was progressively promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ping died, Liu Ji succeeded to the command and was progressively promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奚數侵邊，濟擊走之，窮追千餘里，至青都山，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: The Xi repeatedly raided the border; Ji struck and drove them off, pursued them more than a thousand li to Qingdu Mountain, and beheaded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xi repeatedly raided the frontier, Liu Ji routed them, pursued them more than a thousand li to Qingdu Mountain, and took twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 其後又掠檀、薊北鄙，濟率軍會室韋，破之。

translations.literal: Thereafter they again plundered the northern borders of Tan and Ji; Ji led troops in alliance with the Shiwei and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When they again raided the northern borders of Tan and Ji, Liu Ji led troops in alliance with the Shiwei and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叛，濟合諸將曰：「天子知我怨趙，必命我伐之，趙且大備我，奈何？」

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Ji assembled the generals and said, "The Son of Heaven knows we bear a grudge against Zhao and will surely order us to attack; Zhao will greatly prepare against us—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Liu Ji assembled his generals and said, "The emperor knows we bear a grudge against Zhao and will surely order us to attack; Zhao will prepare heavily against us—what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 裨將譚忠欲激濟伐承宗，疾言曰：「天子不使我伐趙，趙亦不備燕。」

translations.literal: Deputy general Tan Zhong, wishing to incite Ji to attack Chengzong, spoke sharply, saying, "The Son of Heaven will not have us attack Zhao, and Zhao will not prepare against Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Tan Zhong, wishing to spur Liu Ji to attack Chengzong, spoke sharply: "The emperor will not order us to attack Zhao, and Zhao will not prepare against Yan."

sentences.zh: 濟怒，系之。

translations.literal: Ji was angry and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji was furious and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 使視趙，果不設備。

translations.literal: He sent someone to observe Zhao; indeed they made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He sent scouts to Zhao; indeed no preparations had been made.

sentences.zh: 數日，詔書許濟無出師。

translations.literal: Several days later an edict permitted Ji not to dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later an edict arrived permitting Liu Ji not to dispatch troops.

sentences.zh: 濟釋忠，謝而問之，忠曰：「昭義盧從史外親燕，內實忌之；

translations.literal: Ji released Zhong, apologized, and asked him; Zhong said, "Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi outwardly favors Yan but inwardly truly resents it;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji released Tan Zhong, apologized, and asked his reasoning; Tan Zhong said, "Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi outwardly favors Yan but inwardly resents it;

sentences.zh: 外絕趙，內實與之。

translations.literal: outwardly he cuts off Zhao but inwardly is actually allied with it.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly he cuts ties with Zhao but is secretly allied with it.

sentences.zh: 此為趙畫曰：『燕倚趙自固，雖甚怨，必不殘趙，故不足虞也。』

translations.literal: This is the plan he drew for Zhao, saying: 'Yan relies on Zhao to secure itself; though greatly resentful, it will surely not harm Zhao, so there is nothing to fear.'
translations.idiomatic: This is the counsel he gave Zhao: 'Yan relies on Zhao for its security; though deeply resentful, it will surely not harm Zhao, so there is nothing to fear.'

sentences.zh: 趙既不備燕，從史則告天子曰：『燕、趙，宿怨也，今趙見伐而不備燕，是燕反與趙。』

translations.literal: Since Zhao does not prepare against Yan, Congshi then tells the Son of Heaven, saying: 'Yan and Zhao are old enemies; now Zhao is being attacked yet does not prepare against Yan—this means Yan is secretly allied with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhao makes no preparations against Yan, Congshi tells the emperor, 'Yan and Zhao are old enemies; now Zhao is under attack yet makes no preparations against Yan—this means Yan is secretly allied with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 此所以知天子不使君伐趙，趙亦不備燕。」

translations.literal: This is how I know the Son of Heaven will not have you attack Zhao, and Zhao will not prepare against Yan."
translations.idiomatic: That is how I know the emperor will not order you to attack Zhao, and Zhao will not prepare against Yan."

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「計安出？」

translations.literal: Ji said, "What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji asked, "What plan do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「今天子誅承宗，而燕無一卒濟易水者，正使潞人賣恩於趙，販忠於上，是君貯忠誼心，而染私趙之名，卒不見德於趙，惡聲徒嘈嘈於天下。」

translations.literal: He said, "Now the Son of Heaven is punishing Chengzong, yet Yan has not a single soldier crossing the Yi River—this precisely lets the men of Lu sell favor to Zhao and trade loyalty to the sovereign; you would store up a heart of loyalty and righteousness yet be stained with the name of privately favoring Zhao, ultimately receiving no gratitude from Zhao, with ill repute merely clamoring throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The emperor is punishing Chengzong, yet Yan has not sent a single soldier across the Yi River—this lets the men of Lu sell favor to Zhao and trade loyalty to the throne; you would hoard loyalty yet be branded as secretly favoring Zhao, win no gratitude from Zhao, and earn only ill repute throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 濟然之，以兵七萬先諸軍，斬首數千級，又拔饒陽，屯瀛州。

translations.literal: Ji approved; with seventy thousand troops he preceded the other armies, beheaded several thousand, also captured Raoyang, and encamped at Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji agreed; he marched ahead of the other armies with seventy thousand men, took several thousand heads, captured Raoyang, and encamped at Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進攻安平，久不拔，濟命次子總以兵八千先登，日中拔其城。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Anping, they could not capture it for a long time; Ji ordered his second son Zong with eight thousand troops to scale first, and by midday the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Anping, they failed to capture it for a long time; Liu Ji ordered his second son Liu Zong with eight thousand men to lead the assault, and by midday the city fell.

sentences.zh: 會赦承宗，進中書令。

translations.literal: When Chengzong was pardoned, Ji was promoted to head of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong was pardoned, Liu Ji was promoted to head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 濟之出，以長子緄攝留務，總為行營都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Ji went out on campaign, he had his eldest son Wen manage affairs in his absence, and Zong served as commander-in-chief of the campaign army knowing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji marched out, he left his eldest son Liu Wen in charge of affairs and appointed Liu Zong commander of the campaign army.

sentences.zh: 濟病甚，總與左右張玘、成國寶及帳內親近謀殺濟，乃使人詐從京師來，曰：「朝廷以公前屯瀛州逗留，詔副大使代節度。」

translations.literal: Ji was gravely ill; Zong, together with his attendants Zhang Qi, Cheng Guobao, and close associates within the tent, plotted to kill Ji; they had someone falsely come from the capital, saying, "The court, because you previously halted at Ying Prefecture and delayed, has ordered the deputy commissioner to replace you in the military commission."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji fell gravely ill; Liu Zong, together with his attendants Zhang Qi, Cheng Guobao, and close associates, plotted to kill him; they sent a false messenger from the capital saying, "The court, because you halted at Ying Prefecture, has ordered the deputy commissioner to replace you."

sentences.zh: 明日，復使人曰：「詔節至太原矣。」

translations.literal: The next day they again sent someone saying, "The edict staff has reached Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The next day another messenger said, "The edict staff has reached Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 又使人走呼曰：「過代矣。」

translations.literal: Again they sent someone running and shouting, "It has passed Dai!"
translations.idiomatic: Another ran shouting, "It has passed Dai!"

sentences.zh: 舉軍驚。

translations.literal: The entire army was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 濟憤且怒，不知所為，誅主兵大將數十人及素與緄厚善者，亟追緄，以玨已兄臯代留事。

translations.literal: Ji was both angry and enraged, not knowing what to do; he executed several dozen chief military generals and those who had long been close to Wen, urgently pursued Wen, and had Qi and his elder brother Gao replace affairs in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, furious and bewildered, executed several dozen chief generals and those close to Liu Wen, urgently recalled Liu Wen, and had Zhang Qi and his elder brother Gao take charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 濟自朝至中昃不食，渴索酏漿，總使吏唐弘實寘毒，濟飲而死，年五十四。

translations.literal: From morning until midday Ji ate nothing; thirsty, he asked for fermented milk; Zong had the clerk Tang Hongshi place poison in it, and Ji drank and died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until midday Liu Ji ate nothing; thirsty, he asked for fermented milk; Liu Zong had the clerk Tang Hongshi poison it, and Liu Ji drank and died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 緄至涿州，總矯濟命殺之。

translations.literal: When Wen reached Zhuo Prefecture, Zong forged Ji's order and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wen reached Zhuo Prefecture, Liu Zong forged Liu Ji's order and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 乃發喪，贈太師，謚曰莊武。

translations.literal: He then announced the mourning; Ji was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He then announced the mourning; Liu Ji was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 總性陰賊，尤險譎，已毒父，即領軍政，朝廷不知其奸，故詔嗣節度，封楚國公，進累檢校司空。

translations.literal: Zong by nature was sinister and treacherous, especially cunning and deceitful; having already poisoned his father, he immediately assumed military and civil command; the court did not know his treachery, and therefore ordered him to succeed to the commission, enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and progressively promoted him to acting minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong was by nature sinister and treacherous, especially cunning and deceitful; having poisoned his father, he immediately assumed command; the court unaware of his crime ordered him to succeed, enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and progressively promoted him to acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 承宗再拒命，總遣兵取武強，按軍兩端，以私饋賫。

translations.literal: When Chengzong again defied orders, Zong sent troops to take Wuqiang, kept his army hedging both sides, and sent private gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong again defied the court, Liu Zong sent troops to take Wuqiang, kept his army hedging both sides, and sent private gifts to both parties.

sentences.zh: 憲宗知之，外示崇寵，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong knew this and outwardly showed great favor, promoting him to co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong knew this but outwardly showed great favor, promoting him to co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及吳元濟、李師道平，承宗憂死，田弘正入鎮州，總失支助，大恐，謀自安。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji and Li Shidao were pacified, Chengzong died of worry, Tian Hongzheng entered Zhen Prefecture, Zong lost his support, was greatly afraid, and plotted to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji and Li Shidao were pacified, Chengzong died of anxiety, Tian Hongzheng entered Zhen Prefecture, Liu Zong lost his backers, was terrified, and plotted to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 又數見父兄為崇，乃衣食浮屠數百人，晝夜祈禳，而總憩祠場則暫安，或居臥內，輒驚不能寐。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly saw his father and elder brother as spirits; he therefore clothed and fed several hundred Buddhist monks, praying day and night for exorcism, and only when Zong rested at the shrine grounds was he briefly at ease; when he dwelt in his bedchamber he would startle awake and could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly saw visions of his father and brother as spirits; he clothed and fed several hundred Buddhist monks, praying day and night for exorcism, and only when resting at the shrine grounds was he briefly at ease; in his bedchamber he would start awake and could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 晚年益慘悸，請剔發，衣浮屠服，欲祓除之。

translations.literal: In his later years he grew ever more fearful and alarmed; he requested to have his head shaved, wore Buddhist robes, and wished to exorcise the evil.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew ever more haunted and fearful; he had his head shaved, wore Buddhist robes, and sought exorcism.

sentences.zh: 譚忠復說總曰：「天地之數，合必離，離必合。

translations.literal: Tan Zhong again persuaded Zong, saying, "The numbers of Heaven and Earth: what joins must part, and what parts must join.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong again counseled Liu Zong: "Heaven and earth follow a pattern: what joins must part, and what parts must join.

sentences.zh: 河北與天下離六十年，數窮必合。

translations.literal: Hebei and the realm have been apart for sixty years; when the number is exhausted they must reunite.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei has been separate from the empire for sixty years; when that cycle runs its course, reunion is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 往朱泚、希烈自立，趙、冀、齊、魏稱王，郡國弄兵，低目相視，可謂危矣，然卒於無事。

translations.literal: In the past Zhu Ci and Xilie declared themselves, Zhao, Ji, Qi, and Wei took royal titles, commanderies and states played with arms and looked askance at one another—it could be called perilous—yet in the end nothing came of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Zhu Ci and Li Xilie declared themselves, Zhao, Ji, Qi, and Wei proclaimed kingship, and the provinces bristled with arms and glared at one another—it seemed perilous indeed—yet in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 元和以來，劉辟、李锜、田季安、盧從史、齊、蔡之強，或首於都市，或身為逐客，皆君自見。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanhe era, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Tian Ji'an, Lu Congshi, Qi, and Cai were powerful; some lost their heads in the capital markets, others became exiles—you have seen it all yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanhe era, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Tian Ji'an, Lu Congshi, and the strongmen of Qi and Cai—some lost their heads in the capital markets, others became exiles—you have seen it all yourself.

sentences.zh: 今兵骎骎北來，趙人已獻德、棣十二城，助魏破齊，唯燕無一日勞，後世得無事乎？

translations.literal: Now troops are pressing northward; the men of Zhao have already surrendered twelve cities of De and Di, helped Wei defeat Qi—only Yan has not toiled a single day; can later generations remain uninvolved?
translations.idiomatic: Now imperial troops are pressing north; Zhao has surrendered twelve cities in De and Di and helped Wei defeat Qi—only Yan has not lifted a finger; can later generations remain untouched?

sentences.zh: 為君憂之。」

translations.literal: I worry for you, my lord."
translations.idiomatic: I worry for you, my lord."

sentences.zh: 總泣且謝，因上疏願奉朝請，且欲割所治為三；

translations.literal: Zong wept and thanked him, then submitted a memorial wishing to attend court as a regular official and also wishing to divide his domain into three parts;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong wept and thanked him, then submitted a memorial offering to attend court as a regular official and to divide his domain into three commands;

sentences.zh: 以幽、涿、營為一府，請張弘靖治之；

translations.literal: You, Zhuo, and Ying as one command, requesting Zhang Hongjing to govern it;
translations.idiomatic: You, Zhuo, and Ying as one command, to be governed by Zhang Hongjing;

sentences.zh: 瀛、莫為一府，盧士玫治之；

translations.literal: Ying and Mo as one command, Lu Shimei to govern it;
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Mo as one command, to be governed by Lu Shimei;

sentences.zh: 平、薊、媯、檀為一府，薛平治之。

translations.literal: Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan as one command, Xue Ping to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan as one command, to be governed by Xue Ping.

sentences.zh: 盡籍宿將薦諸朝。

translations.literal: He fully registered veteran generals and recommended them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He registered all veteran generals and recommended them to the court.

sentences.zh: 會穆宗沖逸，宰相崔植、杜元穎無遠謀，欲寵弘靖，重其權，故全付總地，唯分瀛、莫置觀察使。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Muzong was young and carefree; Grand Counselors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying lacked far-sighted plans, wished to favor Hongjing and increase his authority, and therefore fully handed over Zong's territory, only separating Ying and Mo to establish a surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong was young and carefree; Grand Counselors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying lacked foresight, wished to favor Zhang Hongjing and increase his authority, and therefore handed over all of Liu Zong's territory, separating only Ying and Mo under a surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 拜總檢校司徒兼侍中、天平節度使。

translations.literal: Zong was appointed acting grand marshal and attendant-in-chief, military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong was appointed acting grand marshal and attendant-in-chief, military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 又賜浮屠服，號大覺，榜其第為佛祠，遣使者以節、印偕來。

translations.literal: He was also granted Buddhist robes, given the title Great Awakening, his residence was posted as a Buddhist shrine, and envoys were sent bringing the staff of office and seal together.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted Buddhist robes, given the title Great Awakening, his residence was converted into a Buddhist shrine, and envoys were sent bearing the staff of office and seal.

sentences.zh: 時總已自髡祝，讓節、印，遂衣浮屠服。

translations.literal: By then Zong had already shaved his head and taken vows, declined the staff and seal, and then wore Buddhist robes.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liu Zong had already shaved his head and taken vows, declined the staff and seal, and donned Buddhist robes.

sentences.zh: 行及定州，卒。

translations.literal: When he reached Ding Prefecture on the journey, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died when he reached Ding Prefecture on the journey.

sentences.zh: 始，總請代，獻馬萬五千匹，群臣或疑其詐，帝獨納之，使給事中薛存慶宣慰，給所部復一歲，緡錢百萬勞軍，高年惸獨不能自存者，官吏就問，賜粟帛。

translations.literal: At first, when Zong requested to be replaced, he presented fifteen thousand horses; some ministers suspected deceit, but the Emperor alone accepted it, sent Supervising Secretary Xue Cunqing to proclaim consolation, granted his domain tax exemption for another year, a million strings of cash to reward the army, and for the aged and solitary who could not support themselves, officials were sent to inquire and grant grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong first offered to surrender his command, he presented fifteen thousand horses; some ministers suspected deceit, but the emperor alone accepted, sent Supervising Secretary Xue Cunqing to proclaim consolation, granted his domain tax exemption for another year, a million strings of cash to reward the army, and dispatched officials to grant grain and cloth to the aged and destitute who could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 總遂與忠俱行，軍中世懷其惠，擁留不得進。

translations.literal: Zong then set out together with Zhong; the army, having long benefited from his kindness, crowded around and detained him so he could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong then set out with Tan Zhong; the army, long grateful for his kindness, crowded around and detained him so he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 總殺首謀者十人，以節付張臯，夜間道去，遲明，軍中乃知。

translations.literal: Zong killed ten ringleaders, handed the staff of office to Zhang Gao, and departed by night on a side road; at dawn the army only then learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong executed ten ringleaders, handed the staff of office to Zhang Gao, and slipped away by night on a side road; at dawn the army only then learned he was gone.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子礎及弟約至長安者十一人，皆擢州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Chu and younger brothers who reached Chang'an, eleven in all, were all promoted to prefect of a province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Chu and younger brothers who reached Chang'an—eleven in all—were all promoted to provincial prefect.

sentences.zh: 忠護總喪至，亦卒。

translations.literal: Zhong escorted Zong's coffin to its destination and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong escorted Liu Zong's coffin to its destination and also died.

sentences.zh: 忠，絳人，喜兵，善謀事，蓋健男子雲。

translations.literal: Zhong was a man of Jiang, fond of military affairs and skilled at plotting—truly a robust man, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong was a man of Jiang, fond of military affairs and skilled at strategy—a robust and capable man, it is said.

sentences.zh: 朱克融，滔孫也。

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong was Tao's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong was Zhu Tao's grandson.

sentences.zh: 以偏校事劉總。

translations.literal: As a deputy officer he served Liu Zong.
translations.idiomatic: As a deputy officer he served Liu Zong.

sentences.zh: 總將入朝，慮後有變，籍其軍材勇與黠暴不制者，悉薦之朝，冀厚與爵位，使北方歆艷，無甘亂心，克融在遣。

translations.literal: When Zong was about to enter court, fearing future trouble, he registered the army's talented and brave along with the cunning, violent, and uncontrollable, and recommended them all to the court, hoping to grant them rich ranks and titles so the north would admire and envy them and have no taste for rebellion; Kerong was among those sent.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong prepared to enter court, fearing future trouble, he registered the army's brave and talented along with the cunning and violent, and recommended them all to the court, hoping rich ranks would make the north admire and envy them and lose taste for rebellion; Kerong was among those sent.

sentences.zh: 方是時，執政非其人，既見總納地，謂天下曠然無復事。

translations.literal: At that time those in power were not the right men; seeing that Zong had surrendered his territory, they thought the realm was suddenly free of further affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the wrong men held power; seeing Liu Zong surrender his territory, they thought the realm was suddenly free of further trouble.

sentences.zh: 克融等留京師，久之不得調，數詣宰相求自試，皆不聽，羸色敗服，饑寒無所貣丐，內怨忿。

translations.literal: Kerong and the others remained in the capital; for a long time they received no appointments; they repeatedly visited grand counselors requesting trial assignments, but none were granted; emaciated in appearance and in tattered clothes, hungry and cold with nowhere to borrow or beg, they nursed resentment inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong and the others remained in the capital; for a long time they received no appointments; they repeatedly petitioned grand counselors for trial assignments but were refused; emaciated and in tattered clothes, hungry and cold with nowhere to turn, they nursed bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 會張弘靖赴鎮，因悉遣還。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hongjing went to his command, they were all sent back on that occasion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hongjing departed for his command, they were all sent back.

sentences.zh: 明年，陷弓高，攻下博，與王廷湊共圍深州。

translations.literal: The next year he captured Gonggao, attacked Xiabo, and together with Wang Tingcou besieged Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he captured Gonggao, attacked Xiabo, and together with Wang Tingcou besieged Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 裴度以檄譙諭，克融乃還，因進檢校工部尚書，表獻馬萬匹、羊十萬，請直賞軍。

translations.literal: Pei Du with a proclamation reproached and admonished him; Kerong then returned, was promoted to acting minister of works, and memorialized presenting ten thousand horses and a hundred thousand sheep, requesting cash payment to reward the army.
