translations.idiomatic: Pei Du reproached him in a proclamation; Kerong then withdrew, was promoted to acting minister of works, and memorialized presenting ten thousand horses and a hundred thousand sheep, requesting cash to reward his army.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，遷檢校司空，賜邊屯時服，克融以帛疏惡，囚詔使楊文端以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jingzong's reign he was promoted to acting minister of works; seasonal garments for frontier garrisons were granted; Kerong, finding the silks coarse and inferior, imprisoned the edict envoy Yang Wenduan to report it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Jingzong's reign he was promoted to acting minister of works; when seasonal garments for frontier garrisons were granted, Kerong, finding the silks coarse and inferior, imprisoned the edict envoy Yang Wenduan to report it.

sentences.zh: 又上言：「聞陛下東幸雒，願率匠丁五千助營宮室，迎乘輿，且請帛三十萬，備一歲費。」

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial, saying, "Hearing that Your Majesty will travel east to Luo, I wish to lead five thousand craftsmen to help build palace halls and welcome the imperial carriage, and also request three hundred thousand bolts of silk to cover one year's expenses."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Hearing that Your Majesty will travel east to Luoyang, I wish to lead five thousand craftsmen to help build palace halls and welcome the imperial carriage, and request three hundred thousand bolts of silk for one year's expenses."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，用裴度謀，忍不問，以好言答之，屈其謀，進爵吳興郡王。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; following Pei Du's plan, he endured without inquiry, answered with kind words, thwarted his scheme, and promoted his rank to Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; following Pei Du's counsel, he endured without inquiry, answered with kind words, thwarted the scheme, and promoted Kerong to Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 是年，軍亂，殺克融及其子延齡，詔贈司徒。

translations.literal: That year the army mutinied and killed Kerong and his son Yanling; an edict posthumously granted him grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: That year the army mutinied and killed Kerong and his son Yanling; an edict posthumously granted him grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 次子延嗣立，領留後，為大將李載義殺而代之，並族其家。

translations.literal: The second son Yansi succeeded, assumed acting command, was killed and replaced by the great general Li Zaiyi, who also exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yansi succeeded as acting commander but was killed and replaced by the great general Li Zaiyi, who also exterminated his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 李載義，自稱恒山湣王之後。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi claimed to be a descendant of the Min King of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi claimed descent from the Min King of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 性矜蕩，好與豪傑遊，力挽強搏鬥。

translations.literal: By nature he was proud and unrestrained, fond of associating with heroes, and strong at drawing the bow and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was proud and unrestrained, fond of associating with bold men, and strong at archery and wrestling.

sentences.zh: 劉濟在幽州，高其能，引補帳下，從征伐，積多為牙中兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji was in Youzhou, he valued his ability, recruited him to serve under his banner, followed on campaigns, and through accumulated merit became commander of military affairs in the guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji held Youzhou, he valued Li Zaiyi's ability, recruited him to his staff, followed him on campaigns, and through accumulated merit rose to commander of military affairs in the guard.

sentences.zh: 朱克融死，子延嗣叛命，殘用其人。

translations.literal: When Zhu Kerong died, his son Yansi defied orders and cruelly exploited his men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kerong died, his son Yansi defied the court and cruelly exploited his men.

sentences.zh: 載義因眾不忍，殺之，暴其罪於朝。

translations.literal: Zaiyi, because the troops could not endure it, killed him and exposed his crimes to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi, because the troops could not endure Yansi's cruelty, killed him and reported his crimes to the court.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即授檢校戶部尚書、盧龍軍節度使，封武威郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong immediately appointed him acting minister of revenue, military commissioner of the Lulong Army, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong immediately appointed him acting minister of revenue and military commissioner of the Lulong Army, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 初，張弘靖之囚，幕府多見害，妻子留不遣。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhang Hongjing was imprisoned, many in his staff were harmed and wives and children were detained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hongjing was imprisoned, many of his staff were killed and their wives and children were detained.

sentences.zh: 及是，載義悉護送京師，雖僮廝畢行。

translations.literal: At this time Zaiyi fully escorted them all to the capital, even servants going entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi then escorted them all to the capital, even the servants.

sentences.zh: 俄而李同捷據滄、景，邀襲封，載義請討賊自效，文宗嘉之，進檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: Before long Li Tongjie held Cang and Jing and intercepted and attacked Feng; Zaiyi requested to campaign against the bandits to prove his loyalty; Emperor Wenzong praised this and promoted him to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Tongjie held Cang and Jing and raided Feng; Li Zaiyi volunteered to campaign against the rebels; Emperor Wenzong praised this and promoted him to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 斬級數有功，賊平，詔同中書門下平章事，賜白玉帶，示殊禮。

translations.literal: He beheaded many enemies with repeated merit; when the bandits were pacified, an edict made him co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, granted a white jade belt, showing special honor.
translations.idiomatic: He took many enemy heads with repeated distinction; when the rebels were pacified, an edict made him co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat and granted a white jade belt as a special honor.

sentences.zh: 大和四年，為兵馬使楊誌誠所逐，奔易州，即上言：「自破滄州賊，屢請朝不許，今願將妻子身入見。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dahe he was driven out by military commissioner Yang Zhicheng, fled to Yi Prefecture, and immediately submitted a memorial, saying, "Since defeating the Cangzhou bandits I have repeatedly requested audience but was not permitted; now I wish to bring my wife and children and come in person to see Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: In 830 he was driven out by military commissioner Yang Zhicheng, fled to Yi Prefecture, and memorialized: "Since defeating the Cangzhou rebels I have repeatedly requested audience but was refused; now I wish to bring my wife and children and come in person to see Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝令使者抵太原尉迎，賜袍笏裝器；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered envoys to meet him at the Taiyuan post station, granting robes, tablet, and travel gear;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered envoys to meet him at the Taiyuan post station and granted robes, tablet, and travel gear;

sentences.zh: 又以其嘗有功，且意恭順，乃冊拜太保，仍平章事。

translations.literal: also because he had once had merit and was deemed respectful and obedient, he was then appointed Grand Guardian and retained as co-director.
translations.idiomatic: and because he had once served with merit and seemed respectful and obedient, he was appointed Grand Guardian and retained as co-director.

sentences.zh: 俄為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he became military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 徙河東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 始，回鶻使者歲入朝，所過暴慢，吏不敢何禁，但嚴兵自守。

translations.literal: At first, Uyghur envoys entered court each year; wherever they passed they were violent and insolent; officials dared not restrain them and only maintained strict troops for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur envoys entered court each year; wherever they passed they were violent and insolent; officials dared not restrain them and only maintained strict guard.

sentences.zh: 虜忸習，益謷悍，至鞭候人，剽突市區。

translations.literal: The barbarians, accustomed to indulgence, grew ever more arrogant and fierce, even whipping relay attendants and raiding market districts.
translations.idiomatic: Accustomed to indulgence, they grew ever more arrogant and fierce, even whipping relay attendants and raiding market districts.

sentences.zh: 時大酋李暢者，曉華人語，尤兇黠。

translations.literal: At that time the great chieftain Li Chang understood Chinese speech and was especially fierce and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great chieftain Li Chang understood Chinese and was especially fierce and cunning.

sentences.zh: 既就館，橫須索，抶{疒只}郵人。

translations.literal: Once he reached the guest lodge, he made unreasonable demands and beat the relay attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once lodged at the guest house, he made unreasonable demands and beat the relay attendants.

sentences.zh: 載義召暢語曰：「可汗以舅甥故，使將軍朝貢，誼不容將軍暴也。

translations.literal: Zaiyi summoned Chang and said, "The Qaghan, because of the uncle-nephew bond, sent the General to pay tribute; propriety does not permit the General to act violently.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi summoned Li Chang and said, "The Qaghan, because of the uncle-nephew bond, sent you to pay tribute; propriety does not permit you to act violently.

sentences.zh: 天子厚饔餼以禮客，有不謹，吏皆論死。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven generously provides feasts to honor guests as ritual demands; for any lack of propriety, officials are all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor generously feasts guests as ritual demands; for any breach of propriety, officials are sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 若將軍所部不戢，而奪攘自如，我必殺所犯者，將軍其少戒。」

translations.literal: If the General's followers are not restrained and plunder as they please, I will surely kill the offenders—General, take some warning."
translations.idiomatic: If your followers are not restrained and plunder as they please, I will kill the offenders—General, take warning."

sentences.zh: 因悉罷所防兵，以兩卒護闔。

translations.literal: He then fully dismissed the guarding troops and had only two soldiers protect the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed all guarding troops and posted only two soldiers at the gate.

sentences.zh: 暢嚴憚之，訖無犯者。

translations.literal: Chang was deeply in awe of him, and in the end there were no offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang was deeply intimidated, and in the end there were no further offenses.

sentences.zh: 進兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrently serve as attendant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrently serve as attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 會吏下請立碑紀功，詔李程為之辭，未有字。

translations.literal: When officials below requested a stele to record his merit, an edict had Li Cheng compose the text, but no courtesy name had yet been given.
translations.idiomatic: When officials requested a stele to record his merit, an edict had Li Cheng compose the text, but no courtesy name had yet been given.

sentences.zh: 帝詔曰：「《周書》『凡厥正人，既富方谷。』

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict, "The Book of Zhou says, 'For all upright men, when enriched, give them Fanggu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict, "The Book of Zhou says, 'For all upright men, when enriched, give them Fanggu.

sentences.zh: 卿宜當之，以方谷為字。」

translations.literal: You should be worthy of this; take Fanggu as your courtesy name."
translations.idiomatic: You are worthy of this; take Fanggu as your courtesy name."

sentences.zh: 其寵待如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 開成二年卒，年五十，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he died, aged fifty; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 837 at fifty; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，載義母葬范陽，為楊誌誠掘發。

translations.literal: At first, Zaiyi's mother was buried at Fanyang and was exhumed by Yang Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi's mother had been buried at Fanyang and was exhumed by Yang Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 後誌誠被逐，道太原，載義奏請剔其心，償母怨，不許。

translations.literal: Later when Zhicheng was driven out and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi memorialized requesting to cut out his heart to avenge his mother's grievance, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Zhicheng was driven out and passed through Taiyuan, Li Zaiyi memorialized requesting to cut out his heart to avenge his mother, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺之，官屬苦救乃免，然盡戕其妻息士卒，其天資驕暴雲，帝屈法弗劾也。

translations.literal: He also wished to kill him; officials strenuously intervened to save him, yet Zaiyi slaughtered all his wives, children, and soldiers; such was his inborn arrogance and violence, it is said—the Emperor bent the law and did not prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to kill Zhicheng; officials strenuously intervened to save him, yet Li Zaiyi slaughtered all his wives, children, and soldiers—such was his inborn arrogance and violence, it is said—the emperor bent the law and did not prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 誌誠者，事載義為牙將。

translations.literal: Zhicheng had served Zaiyi as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng had served Li Zaiyi as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 載義宴天子使者鞠場，誌誠與其黨噪而起，載義走，因自為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Zaiyi entertained the Son of Heaven's envoy at the cuju field, Zhicheng and his faction rose up with a clamor; Zaiyi fled, and Zhicheng then made himself commander-in-chief knowing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zaiyi entertained the emperor's envoy at the cuju field, Zhicheng and his faction rose in uproar; Li Zaiyi fled, and Zhicheng made himself commander of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 文宗更以嘉王領節度，用誌誠為留後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong changed to have Prince Jia hold the military commission and used Zhicheng as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong appointed Prince Jia nominal military commissioner and Zhicheng acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校工部尚書，擢節度副大使。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting minister of works and promoted to deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting minister of works and promoted to deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進檢校吏部。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to acting minister of civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was promoted to acting minister of civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔下，邸吏白宰相曰：「軍中不識朝廷儀，惟知尚書改仆射為進秩。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the relay clerk informed the grand counselor, saying, "The army does not understand court protocol; they only know that changing from minister to vice director is a promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the relay clerk informed the grand counselor: "The army does not understand court protocol; they only know that changing from minister to vice director is a promotion.

sentences.zh: 今一府盛服以待天子命，如復為尚書，則舉軍慚，使者勢不得出。」

translations.literal: Now the entire command is in full dress awaiting the Son of Heaven's order; if he is again made minister, the whole army will be shamed and the envoy will likely be unable to depart."
translations.idiomatic: The entire command is in full dress awaiting the emperor's order; if he is again made minister, the whole army will be shamed and the envoy will likely be unable to depart."

sentences.zh: 既誌誠果怨望，軍有謾言，囚中人魏寶義及它使焦奉鸞、尹士恭，而遣部將王文穎入謝，讓還所命。

translations.literal: Since Zhicheng was indeed resentful, there was slander in the army; he imprisoned the eunuch Wei Baoyi and other envoys Jiao Fengluan and Yin Shigong, and sent his officer Wang Wenying to enter court to apologize and return the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng was indeed resentful; there was slander in the army; he imprisoned the eunuch Wei Baoyi and envoys Jiao Fengluan and Yin Shigong, and sent his officer Wang Wenying to court to apologize and return the appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝復賜之，文穎不肯受，輒去。

translations.literal: The Emperor again granted the appointment; Wenying refused to accept it and simply departed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again granted the appointment; Wenying refused to accept it and simply departed.

sentences.zh: 帝忍不責，乃遣使進檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: The Emperor endured without blame and then sent envoys to promote him to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endured without blame and sent envoys to promote him to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，為下所逐，推部將史元忠總留後。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was driven out by his subordinates, who promoted the officer Shi Yuanzhong to overall acting command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was driven out by his subordinates, who installed the officer Shi Yuanzhong as overall acting commander.

sentences.zh: 誌誠在鎮，密制天子袞冕，其被服皆擬乘輿。

translations.literal: While Zhicheng held the command, he secretly had the Son of Heaven's ceremonial robes made; his garments all imitated the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhicheng held command, he secretly had imperial ceremonial robes made; his garments all imitated the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 元忠表而暴於朝，詔御史按治，斥嶺南，至商州，誅之，而以通王領節度，授元忠留後。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong memorialized and exposed this to the court; an edict ordered censors to investigate, banish him to Lingnan; at Shang Prefecture he was executed, and Prince Tong was made to hold the commission while Yuanzhong was granted acting command.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong memorialized and exposed this to the court; censors were ordered to investigate and banish him to Lingnan; at Shang Prefecture he was executed, Prince Tong was made nominal commissioner, and Yuanzhong was granted acting command.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校工部尚書，為副大使。

translations.literal: The next year he was acting minister of works and made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed acting minister of works and deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，為偏將陳行泰所殺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was killed by the deputy general Chen Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huichang era he was killed by the deputy general Chen Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 行泰邀節制，未報。

translations.literal: Xingtai demanded the military commission; no response had yet come.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xingtai demanded the military commission; no response had yet come.

sentences.zh: 次將張絳殺行泰，起求帥軍，武宗自用張仲武代之。

translations.literal: The next officer Zhang Jiang killed Xingtai, rose up to request command of the army, and Emperor Wuzong himself used Zhang Zhongwu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The next officer Zhang Jiang killed Chen Xingtai and demanded command of the army; Emperor Wuzong himself appointed Zhang Zhongwu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 張仲武，范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，為雄武軍使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huichang era he was commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 行泰殺元忠，宰相李德裕計：河朔請帥，皆報下太速，故軍得以安，若少須下，且有變。

translations.literal: When Xingtai killed Yuanzhong, Grand Counselor Li Deyu calculated: when Hebei requested a commander, responses were always issued too quickly, so the army could settle; if issued slightly later, there would be trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xingtai killed Yuanzhong, Grand Counselor Li Deyu calculated: when Hebei requested a commander, responses were always issued too quickly, allowing the army to settle; if delayed slightly, there would be trouble.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，未報，果為絳所殺，復誘其軍以請，亦置未報。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed; before a response came, Xingtai was indeed killed by Jiang, who again incited the army to request command; this too was left unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; before a response came, Chen Xingtai was indeed killed by Zhang Jiang, who again incited the army to request command; this too was left unanswered.

sentences.zh: 是時，回鶻為黠戛斯所破，烏介可汗托天德塞上，而仲武遣其屬吳仲舒入朝，請以本軍擊回鶻。

translations.literal: At that time the Uyghurs were defeated by the Kirghiz; Qaghan Wujie took refuge at the Tiantde frontier pass, and Zhongwu sent his subordinate Wu Zhongshu to court requesting to use his army to attack the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Uyghurs were defeated by the Kirghiz; Qaghan Wujie took refuge at the Tiantde frontier pass, and Zhang Zhongwu sent his subordinate Wu Zhongshu to court requesting to use his army against the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 德裕因問北方事，仲舒曰：「行泰、絳皆遊客，人心不附。

translations.literal: Deyu therefore inquired about northern affairs; Zhongshu said, "Xingtai and Jiang are both outsiders; the people's hearts do not attach to them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu inquired about northern affairs; Wu Zhongshu said, "Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang are both outsiders; the troops do not attach to them.

sentences.zh: 仲武，舊將張光朝子，年五十餘，通書，習戎事，性忠義，願歸款朝廷舊矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongwu is the son of the old general Zhang Guangchao, over fifty years old, versed in books, practiced in military affairs, loyal and righteous by nature, and has long wished to submit sincerely to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu is the son of the old general Zhang Guangchao, over fifty, versed in books, practiced in military affairs, loyal and righteous by nature, and has long wished to submit sincerely to the court."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「即以為帥，軍得無復亂乎？」

translations.literal: Deyu said, "If he is immediately made commander, will the army not rebel again?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked, "If he is immediately made commander, will the army not rebel again?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「仲武得士心，受命必有逐絳者。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Zhongwu has won the troops' hearts; once he receives the appointment there will surely be those who drive out Jiang."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zhang Zhongwu has won the troops' loyalty; once he receives the appointment there will surely be those who drive out Zhang Jiang."

sentences.zh: 德裕入白帝曰：「行泰等邀節不可許，仲武求自效，用之有名，軍且無辭。」

translations.literal: Deyu entered and reported to the Emperor, saying, "Xingtai and the others' demand for the commission cannot be granted; Zhongwu seeks to prove his loyalty—using him has justification, and the army will have no complaint."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu reported to the emperor: "Chen Xingtai and the others' demand for the commission cannot be granted; Zhang Zhongwu seeks to prove his loyalty—appointing him is justified, and the army will have no complaint."

sentences.zh: 乃擢兵馬留後，而詔撫王領節度。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to military commissioner acting in command, while an edict had Prince Fu hold the commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to acting military commissioner, while an edict had Prince Fu hold the commission nominally.

sentences.zh: 詔下，絳果為軍中所逐，即拜仲武副大使、檢校工部尚書、蘭陵郡公。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Jiang was indeed driven out by the army; Zhongwu was immediately appointed deputy commissioner, acting minister of works, and Duke of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Zhang Jiang was indeed driven out by the army; Zhang Zhongwu was immediately appointed deputy commissioner, acting minister of works, and Duke of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 會回鶻特勒那頡啜擁赤心部七千帳逼漁陽，仲武使其弟仲至與別將遊奉寰等率銳兵三萬破之，獲馬、牛、橐它、旗纛不勝計，遣吏獻狀，進檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Uyghur tegin Najiachuo led seven thousand tents of the Chixin tribe to press on Yuyang, Zhongwu sent his younger brother Zhongzhi together with the separate general You Fenghuan and others to lead thirty thousand elite troops to defeat them, capturing horses, cattle, camels, banners, and standards beyond counting; he sent officials to present the report and was promoted to acting minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghur tegin Najiachuo led seven thousand tents of the Chixin tribe against Yuyang, Zhang Zhongwu sent his brother Zhongzhi and separate general You Fenghuan with thirty thousand elite troops to rout them, capturing incalculable horses, cattle, camels, banners, and standards; he sent officials to report the victory and was promoted to acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 始，回鶻常有酋長監奚、契丹以督歲貢，因诇刺中國。

translations.literal: At first the Uyghurs always had chieftains supervising the Xi and Khitan to oversee annual tribute, and thereby spied on China.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had long posted chieftains to supervise the Xi and Khitan and collect annual tribute, using the arrangement to spy on China.

sentences.zh: 仲武使裨將石公緒等厚結二部，執諜者八百餘人殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu had his deputy generals Shi Gongxu and others cultivate close ties with the two tribes, seized more than eight hundred spies, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu had his deputies Shi Gongxu and others cultivate close ties with the two tribes, seized more than eight hundred spies, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 回鶻欲入五原，掠保塞雜虜，乃先以宣門將軍四十七人詭好結歡，仲武賂其下，盡得所謀，因逗留不遣，使失師期，回鶻人馬多病死者，由是不敢犯五原塞。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs wished to enter Wuyuan and plunder the mixed barbarians guarding the passes; they first sent forty-seven Xuanmen generals under false pretenses of friendship to establish good relations; Zhongwu bribed their subordinates and learned all their plans; he then detained them without sending them back, causing them to miss the campaign deadline; many Uyghur men and horses sickened and died, and thus they dared not violate the Wuyuan pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs planned to enter Wuyuan and raid the mixed tribes guarding the passes; they first sent forty-seven Xuanmen generals under false pretenses of friendship; Zhang Zhongwu bribed their subordinates, learned all their plans, detained them, and caused them to miss their campaign deadline; many Uyghur men and horses sickened and died, and they dared not violate the Wuyuan pass.

sentences.zh: 烏介失勢，往依康居，盡徙餘種，寄黑車子部。

translations.literal: Wujie lost power, went to rely on Kangju, moved all remaining tribes, and took refuge with the Black Cart tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie lost power, fled to Kangju, moved all remaining tribes, and took refuge with the Black Cart tribe.

sentences.zh: 回鶻遂衰，名王貴種相繼降，捕幾千人。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs then declined; famed kings and noble clans surrendered in succession, and several thousand were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs then declined; famed kings and noble clans surrendered in succession, and several thousand were captured.

sentences.zh: 仲武表請立石以紀聖功，帝詔德裕為銘，揭碑盧龍，以告後世。

translations.literal: Zhongwu memorialized requesting a stele to record the sage achievement; the Emperor ordered Deyu to compose the inscription and erected the stele at Lulong to inform later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu memorialized requesting a stele to record the imperial victory; the emperor ordered Li Deyu to compose the inscription and erected the stele at Lulong for posterity.

sentences.zh: 大中初，又破奚北部及山奚，俘獲雜畜不貲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he again defeated the northern Xi and mountain Xi, capturing mixed livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dazhong era he again defeated the northern Xi and mountain Xi, capturing incalculable livestock.

sentences.zh: 擢累檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to acting grand marshal and co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was progressively promoted to acting grand marshal and co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子直方，以右金吾將軍襲節度留後，俄進副大使。

translations.literal: His son Zhifang, as Right Golden Guard General, succeeded to acting military commission and was soon promoted to deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Zhifang, as Right Golden Guard General, succeeded as acting commissioner and was soon promoted to deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舉動多不法，畏下變起，乃托出畋奔京師。

translations.literal: His conduct was largely unlawful; fearing a mutiny from below, he pretended to go hunting and fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was largely unlawful; fearing a mutiny, he pretended to go hunting and fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍中以張允伸總後務。

translations.literal: The army had Zhang YunShen assume overall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The army installed Zhang Yunshen to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 直方至，宣宗遣使者郊勞，授金吾大將軍，以其族大，給檢校工部尚書俸。

translations.literal: When Zhifang arrived, Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to welcome him outside the suburbs, appointed him Grand Golden Guard General, and because his clan was large, granted him the salary of acting minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhifang arrived, Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to welcome him outside the suburbs, appointed him Grand Golden Guard General, and because his clan was large, granted him the salary of acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 久之，進檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 性暴率，坐以小罪笞殺金吾使，改右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: By nature he was violent and blunt; for a minor offense he beat a Golden Guard envoy to death and was changed to Right Forest Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was violent and blunt; for a minor offense he beat a Golden Guard envoy to death and was reassigned as Right Forest Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 好馳獵，往往設罝罘於道。

translations.literal: He loved to hunt on horseback and often set nets and snares on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to hunt on horseback and often set nets and snares on the roads.

sentences.zh: 當宿衛不時入，下遷驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: When on palace guard duty he did not enter on time and was demoted to general of the Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When on palace guard duty he failed to report on time and was demoted to general of the Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 奴婢細過輒殺，積其罪，貶思州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: For minor faults of servants and maids he would kill them; accumulating his crimes, he was demoted to registrar of Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He killed servants and maids for minor faults; accumulating his crimes, he was demoted to registrar of Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母驚曰：「尚有尊於我子邪？」

translations.literal: His mother exclaimed in alarm, "Is there still someone honored above my son?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother exclaimed in alarm, "Is there still someone honored above my son?"

sentences.zh: 久乃復授羽林統軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again appointed Forest Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was again appointed Forest Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 縱部下為盜，復貶康州司馬。

translations.literal: He let his subordinates act as bandits and was again demoted to military aide of Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He let his subordinates act as bandits and was again demoted to military aide of Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後居東都，弋獵愈甚，洛陽飛鳥皆識之，見必群噪。

translations.literal: Later dwelling in the Eastern Capital, he hunted ever more fiercely; the flying birds of Luoyang all recognized him and would clamor in flocks at his sight.
translations.idiomatic: Later dwelling in the Eastern Capital, he hunted ever more fiercely; Luoyang's birds all recognized him and would clamor in flocks at his sight.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，累進左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: During Qianfu he was progressively promoted to Left Valiant Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu era he was progressively promoted to Left Valiant Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 時鄭畋輔政，頗言：「仲武會昌時功第一，今直方百口不自存，每內燕，以衣敝惡，辭不赴。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Tian assisted in government and spoke at length, saying, "Zhongwu's merit in Huichang was foremost; now Zhifang's hundred mouths cannot support themselves; at each inner banquet, citing worn and shabby clothes, he declines to attend.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Tian assisted in government and spoke at length: "Zhang Zhongwu's merit in Huichang was foremost; now Zhang Zhifang's hundred mouths cannot support themselves; at each inner banquet, citing worn and shabby clothes, he declines to attend.

sentences.zh: 陛下錄功念舊，宜少優假。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty records merit and remembers old service—you should grant him some favor."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty records merit and remembers old service—you should grant him some favor."

sentences.zh: 詔還檢校右仆射，進左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: An edict restored him to acting Right Vice Director and promoted him to Left Golden Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored him to acting Right Vice Director and promoted him to Left Golden Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯京師，直方迎灞上，既而納亡命，謀劫巢報天子，公卿多依之。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, Zhifang welcomed him at Bashang; thereafter he took in fugitives and plotted to seize Chao to report to the Son of Heaven; many grand officials relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, Zhang Zhifang welcomed him at Bashang; thereafter he took in fugitives and plotted to seize Chao to report to the emperor; many grand officials relied on him.

sentences.zh: 賊覺，屠其族。

translations.literal: The bandits discovered this and slaughtered his clan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels discovered this and slaughtered his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 張允伸字逢昌，范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang YunShen, courtesy name Fengchang, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunshen, courtesy name Fengchang, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 世為軍校。

translations.literal: For generations his family served as military officers.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family served as military officers.

sentences.zh: 直方出奔，以都知兵馬使為眾立為留後，天子報可。

translations.literal: When Zhifang fled, as commander knowing military affairs he was established by the troops as acting commissioner; the Son of Heaven approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhifang fled, as commander of military affairs he was installed by the troops as acting commissioner; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校散騎常侍，為節度使，累進檢校司徒、兼太傅、同中書門下平章事，封燕國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting Regular Attendant and made military commissioner, progressively promoted to acting grand marshal, concurrently Grand Tutor, co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting Regular Attendant and military commissioner, progressively promoted to acting grand marshal, concurrently Grand Tutor and co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 龐勛以徐州反，上書欲遣弟允臯領兵討賊，不許。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled at Xuzhou, YunShen submitted a memorial wishing to send his younger brother Yungiao to lead troops to suppress the bandits; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled at Xuzhou, Zhang Yunshen memorialized wishing to send his younger brother Yungiao to lead troops against the rebels; this was refused.

sentences.zh: 上米五十萬斛、鹽二萬斛佐用度，詔嘉美，賜玉帶、寶器、紈錦，進兼侍中。

translations.literal: He presented five hundred thousand hu of grain and twenty thousand hu of salt to assist expenses; an edict praised this, granted a jade belt, precious vessels, and silk brocades, and promoted him to concurrently serve as attendant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He presented five hundred thousand hu of grain and twenty thousand hu of salt to help defray expenses; an edict praised this, granted a jade belt, precious vessels, and silk brocades, and promoted him to concurrently serve as attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 咸通十二年，以疾甚，上節、印，便醫藥，詔聽許，以子簡會為副大使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Xiantong, because his illness was severe, he submitted the staff and seal and requested medicine; an edict granted permission, and his son Jianhui was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 871, gravely ill, he submitted the staff and seal and requested medicine; an edict granted permission, and his son Jianhui was made deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八，贈太尉，謚曰忠烈。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-eight; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-eight; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 允伸性勤儉，下所安賴，未嘗有邊鄙虞。

translations.literal: YunShen was diligent and frugal by nature; subordinates relied on him for security, and there were never frontier alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunshen was diligent and frugal by nature; subordinates relied on him, and there were never frontier alarms during his tenure.

sentences.zh: 子十四人。

translations.literal: He had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 簡會入朝，昆弟多至大將軍、刺史、郡佐者，而軍中推張公素為留後。

translations.literal: Jianhui entered court; many brothers rose to grand general, prefect, or commandery aide; meanwhile the army promoted Zhang Gongsu as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui entered court; many brothers rose to grand general, prefect, or commandery aide; meanwhile the army installed Zhang Gongsu as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 公素，范陽人。

translations.literal: Gongsu was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 以列將事允伸，擢累平州刺史。

translations.literal: As a ranked general he served YunShen and was progressively promoted to prefect of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a ranked general he served Zhang Yunshen and was progressively promoted to prefect of Ping.

sentences.zh: 允伸卒，以兵來會喪，軍士素附其威望，簡會知不可制，即出奔。

translations.literal: When YunShen died, Gongsu came with troops to attend the funeral; the soldiers had long attached to his prestige; Jianhui knew he could not control him and immediately fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yunshen died, Zhang Gongsu came with troops to attend the funeral; the soldiers had long attached to his prestige; Jianhui knew he could not control him and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔公素為節度使，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: An edict made Gongsu military commissioner and promoted him to co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhang Gongsu military commissioner and promoted him to co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 性暴歷，眸子多白，燕人號「白眼相公」。

translations.literal: By nature he was violent and harsh; his eyeballs showed much white, and the people of Yan called him the "White-Eyed Lord Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was violent and harsh; his eyeballs showed much white, and the people of Yan called him the "White-Eyed Lord Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 為李茂勛所襲，奔京師，貶復州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was attacked by Li Maoxun, fled to the capital, and was demoted to registrar of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was attacked by Li Maoxun, fled to the capital, and was demoted to registrar of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李茂勛，本回鶻阿布思之裔。

translations.literal: Li Maoxun was originally a descendant of the Uyghur Abu Si.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maoxun was originally a descendant of the Uyghur Abu Si.

sentences.zh: 張仲武時，與其侯王皆降。

translations.literal: During Zhang Zhongwu's time he and his tribal kings all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhang Zhongwu's time he and his tribal kings all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 資沈勇，善馳射，仲武器之，任以將兵，常乘邊積功，賜姓及名。

translations.literal: Endowed with deep courage, skilled at mounted archery, Zhongwu valued him, entrusted him with commanding troops, and he often rode the frontier accumulating merit; he was granted a surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: Endowed with deep courage and skilled at mounted archery, Zhang Zhongwu valued him, entrusted him with troops, and he accumulated merit on the frontier; he was granted a surname and given name.

sentences.zh: 陳貢言者，燕健將，為納降軍使，軍中素信服，茂勛襲殺之，因舉兵，紿稱貢言反。

translations.literal: Chen Gongyan was a stalwart general of Yan, serving as commissioner of surrendered troops; the army had long trusted and obeyed him; Maoxun attacked and killed him, then raised troops, falsely claiming Gongyan had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongyan was a stalwart Yan general serving as commissioner of surrendered troops; the army had long trusted him; Li Maoxun attacked and killed him, then raised troops, falsely claiming Gongyan had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 公素迎擊不利，走，茂勛入府，眾始悟，因推主州務，以聞，詔即拜節度使。

translations.literal: Gongsu went out to meet the attack unfavorably and fled; Maoxun entered the headquarters; the crowd only then understood; they therefore promoted him to manage prefectural affairs, reported this, and an edict immediately appointed him military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu met the attack poorly and fled; Li Maoxun entered headquarters; the troops only then understood; they installed him to manage affairs, reported this, and an edict immediately appointed him military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄以病自上，詔進尚書右仆射致仕。

translations.literal: Before long, citing illness, he submitted his resignation; an edict promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing illness, he resigned; an edict promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 表子可舉代，遂領留後，進為節度使，擢累檢校太尉。

translations.literal: He memorialized that his son Keju succeed him; Keju then assumed acting command, was promoted to military commissioner, and was progressively elevated to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that his son Keju succeed him; Keju assumed acting command, was promoted to military commissioner, and was progressively elevated to acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 中和末，太原李克用始強大，與定州王處存厚相結，可舉惡其窺山東為己患，乃遣使約吐渾都督赫連鐸、鎮州王镕聯和，揚言易、定本燕、趙屬，得其地，且參有之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhonghe, Li Keyong of Taiyuan began to grow powerful and formed close ties with Wang Chucun of Ding Prefecture; Keju resented his coveting Shandong as a threat to himself; he therefore sent envoys to ally with the Tuyuhun commissioner Helian Duo and Wang Rong of Zhen Prefecture, proclaiming that Yi and Ding originally belonged to Yan and Zhao, and that whoever obtained those lands would share them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhonghe era, Li Keyong of Taiyuan grew powerful and formed close ties with Wang Chucun of Ding; Li Keju resented Keyong's designs on Shandong; he sent envoys to ally with Tuyuhun commissioner Helian Duo and Wang Rong of Zhen, proclaiming that Yi and Ding originally belonged to Yan and Zhao and would be shared among allies.

sentences.zh: 即遣軍司馬韓玄紹擊沙陀藥兒嶺，斬首七千級，殺其將朱耶盡忠等，收牛、馬、器鎧數萬。

translations.literal: He immediately sent army marshal Han Xuanshao to attack the Shatuo at Yao'er Ridge, beheaded seven thousand, killed their generals Zhuye Jinzhong and others, and seized tens of thousands of cattle, horses, weapons, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent army marshal Han Xuanshao to attack the Shatuo at Yao'er Ridge, took seven thousand heads, killed their generals Zhuye Jinzhong and others, and seized tens of thousands of cattle, horses, weapons, and armor.

sentences.zh: 又戰雄武軍，殺獲萬人。

translations.literal: He fought again at the Xiongwu Army and killed and captured ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at the Xiongwu Army and killed and captured ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鐸又破沙陀於蔚州，詔以鐸為雲州刺史，進可舉檢校侍中。

translations.literal: Duo again defeated the Shatuo at Wei Prefecture; an edict made Duo prefect of Yun Prefecture and promoted Keju to acting attendant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo again defeated the Shatuo at Wei Prefecture; an edict made Duo prefect of Yun and promoted Li Keju to acting attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 乃遣票將李全忠率眾六萬圍易州。

translations.literal: He then sent swift general Li Quanzhong to lead sixty thousand troops to besiege Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent swift general Li Quanzhong with sixty thousand troops to besiege Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 镕以兵攻無極，處存求援太原，克用自將赴之，鎮人懼，退保新城，克用急攻之，镕引去，追破之九門。

translations.literal: Rong attacked Wuji with troops; Chucun sought aid from Taiyuan; Keyong personally led troops to the rescue; the men of Zhen were afraid, retreated to defend Xincheng; Keyong pressed the attack fiercely; Rong withdrew and was pursued and defeated at Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong attacked Wuji; Wang Chucun sought aid from Taiyuan; Li Keyong personally led troops to the rescue; the men of Zhen retreated to defend Xincheng; Keyong pressed the attack; Rong withdrew and was routed at Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 易久未下，盧龍將劉仁恭穴地以入，得其城，士卒有驕色；

translations.literal: Yi long could not be taken; the Lulong general Liu Rengong tunneled underground to enter and captured the city; the soldiers showed arrogance;
translations.idiomatic: Yi long resisted capture; Lulong general Liu Rengong tunneled into the city and took it; the soldiers grew arrogant;

sentences.zh: 處存以輕兵三千蒙羊皮，夜布之野，以精騎伏它道，全忠軍望為群羊，爭趨之，處存伏騎發，大敗之，復取易州。

translations.literal: Chucun with three thousand light troops covered themselves in sheepskins and spread them in the open country by night; with elite cavalry ambushed on another route, Quanzhong's army saw what appeared to be a flock of sheep and rushed toward them; Chucun's hidden cavalry sprang forth and inflicted great defeat, recapturing Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun covered three thousand light troops in sheepskins and spread them in the open country by night; with elite cavalry ambushed on another route, Li Quanzhong's army saw what appeared to be a flock of sheep and rushed toward them; Chucun's hidden cavalry sprang forth, routed them, and recaptured Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 全忠遁還，盡失芻糧仗鎧，懼得罪，乃裒餘眾反攻幽州，可舉度不支，引其族登樓自燔死。

translations.literal: Quanzhong fled back, losing all fodder, grain, weapons, and armor; fearing punishment, he gathered remaining troops to counterattack Youzhou; Keju judged he could not hold out, led his clan up a tower, and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanzhong fled back, losing all fodder, grain, weapons, and armor; fearing punishment, he gathered remaining troops to counterattack Youzhou; Li Keju judged he could not hold out, led his clan up a tower, and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 李全忠，范陽人。

translations.literal: Li Quanzhong was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanzhong was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 仕為棣州司馬。

translations.literal: He served as military aide of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military aide of Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有蘆生其室，一尺三節，怪之，以問別駕張建，建曰：「蘆，茅類，生於澤，公茅土兆也。

translations.literal: Reeds grew in his house, one chi with three joints; he found it strange and asked Vice Prefect Zhang Jian; Jian said, "Reeds are of the thatch kind, growing in marshes—this is an omen of enfeoffment with fief soil.
translations.idiomatic: Reeds grew in his house, one chi with three joints; he found it strange and asked Vice Prefect Zhang Jian; Jian said, "Reeds are of the thatch kind, growing in marshes—this is an omen of enfeoffment with fief soil.

sentences.zh: 傳節者其三世乎？」

translations.literal: Will the transmission of the commission last three generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Will the transmission of the commission last three generations?"

sentences.zh: 罷歸，事可舉為牙將。

translations.literal: He left office and returned, serving Keju as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: He left office and returned, serving Li Keju as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 可舉死，眾推為留後。

translations.literal: When Keju died, the crowd promoted him as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keju died, the troops installed him as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，拜節度使，未幾卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangqi he was appointed military commissioner; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 885 he was appointed military commissioner; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 子匡威嗣，領留後，進為使。

translations.literal: His son Kuangwei succeeded, assumed acting command, and was promoted to commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Kuangwei succeeded, assumed acting command, and was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 性豪爽，恃燕、薊勁兵處，軒然有雄天下意。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and generous; relying on Yan and Ji's position of strong troops, he held himself high with ambition to dominate the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and generous; relying on Yan and Ji's strong troops, he held himself high with ambition to dominate the realm.

sentences.zh: 與赫連鐸共攻太原，爭雲、代。

translations.literal: Together with Helian Duo he attacked Taiyuan, contending for Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Helian Duo he attacked Taiyuan, contending for Yun and Dai.

sentences.zh: 李克用使安金俊攻鐸，匡威救鐸，戰蔚州，射金俊殺之，乃共表請討沙陀，而朱全忠亦上言願協力，故張浚因請用兵矣。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent An Jinjun to attack Duo; Kuangwei rescued Duo; fighting at Wei Prefecture, he shot and killed Jinjun; they then jointly memorialized requesting a campaign against the Shatuo; Zhu Quanzhong also submitted words wishing to cooperate; thus Zhang Jun therefore requested deployment of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent An Jinjun to attack Duo; Li Kuangwei rescued Duo; fighting at Wei Prefecture, he shot and killed Jinjun; they jointly memorialized requesting a campaign against the Shatuo; Zhu Quanzhong also offered cooperation; thus Zhang Jun requested deployment of troops.

sentences.zh: 浚敗，克用攻雲州，以騎將薛阿檀為前鋒，設伏河上。

translations.literal: Jun was defeated; Keyong attacked Yun Prefecture, with cavalry general Xue Atan as vanguard, setting an ambush on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was defeated; Li Keyong attacked Yun Prefecture, with cavalry general Xue Atan as vanguard, setting an ambush on the river.

sentences.zh: 鐸以精騎追阿檀，抵河而伏起，乃大敗，禽其將賈塞兒，遂圍雲州，塹而守，分兵出井陘，屯常山，大掠深、趙。

translations.literal: Duo with elite cavalry pursued Atan; reaching the river the ambush sprang up and inflicted great defeat; they captured his general Jia Saier; then they besieged Yun Prefecture, dug trenches and held it, divided troops out through Jingxing Pass, encamped at Changshan, and plundered Shen and Zhao on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo with elite cavalry pursued Atan; reaching the river the ambush sprang up and routed him; they captured his general Jia Saier; then they besieged Yun Prefecture, dug trenches and held it, sent troops through Jingxing Pass, encamped at Changshan, and plundered Shen and Zhao on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 匡威以步騎萬餘援王镕，克用還，因急攻鐸。

translations.literal: Kuangwei with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry aided Wang Rong; Keyong returned and therefore pressed the attack on Duo fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry aided Wang Rong; Li Keyong returned and pressed the attack on Duo fiercely.

sentences.zh: 會食盡，鐸棄州奔匡威。

translations.literal: When provisions ran out, Duo abandoned the prefecture and fled to Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out, Helian Duo abandoned the prefecture and fled to Li Kuangwei.

sentences.zh: 克用取雲州，表石善友為刺史。

translations.literal: Keyong took Yun Prefecture and memorialized to make Shi Shanyou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong took Yun Prefecture and memorialized to appoint Shi Shanyou prefect.

sentences.zh: 鐸本吐谷渾部酋也，開成中，其父率種人三千帳自歸，守雲州十五年。

translations.literal: Duo was originally a chieftain of the Tuyuhun tribe; in the Kaicheng era his father led three thousand tents of tribesmen to surrender voluntarily and guarded Yun Prefecture for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo was originally a Tuyuhun chieftain; in the Kaicheng era his father led three thousand tents of tribesmen to surrender and guarded Yun Prefecture for fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 至是，失其地。

translations.literal: At this time he lost his territory.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he lost his territory.

sentences.zh: 景福初，镕誘太原將李存孝降之，克用怒，伐镕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Rong induced Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao to defect to him; Keyong was angry and campaigned against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingfu era, Wang Rong induced Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao to defect; Li Keyong was furious and campaigned against Rong.

sentences.zh: 镕來求救，匡威遣將赴之，克用去。

translations.literal: Rong came seeking rescue; Kuangwei sent generals to go to his aid; Keyong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong sought rescue; Li Kuangwei sent generals to his aid; Li Keyong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，兵復出井陘，匡威自將援镕，將行，置酒大會。

translations.literal: The next year troops again came out through Jingxing Pass; Kuangwei personally led troops to aid Rong; before departing he set out wine at a grand assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The following year troops again came out through Jingxing Pass; Li Kuangwei personally led troops to aid Rong; before departing he held a grand farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 其弟兵馬留後、檢校司徒匡籌妻張，國艷，匡威酒酣，報之，弟怒，匡威軍次博野，乃據城自為留後。

translations.literal: His younger brother, military commissioner acting in command and acting grand marshal Kuangchou's wife Zhang was a national beauty; Kuangwei, deep in wine, violated her; his brother was enraged; Kuangwei's army halted at Boye; Kuangchou then seized the city and made himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kuangchou, acting military commissioner and acting grand marshal, had a wife Zhang of national beauty; Li Kuangwei, deep in wine, violated her; his brother was enraged; Li Kuangwei's army halted at Boye; Kuangchou seized the city and made himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天子即授檢校太保，為節度使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven immediately appointed him acting Grand Guardian and made him military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately appointed him acting Grand Guardian and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 匡威麾下多去，屏營無所歸，留深州，遣其屬李抱貞上書願入朝。

translations.literal: Most of Kuangwei's followers departed; he camped in isolation with nowhere to go, remained at Shen Prefecture, and sent his subordinate Li Baozhen to submit a memorial wishing to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Li Kuangwei's followers departed; he camped in isolation with nowhere to go, remained at Shen Prefecture, and sent his subordinate Li Baozhen to memorialize wishing to enter court.

sentences.zh: 時京師數寇難，人人危懼，傳言金頭王且來，皆亡竄山谷。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had suffered repeated raids and calamities; everyone was in fear; rumor spread that the Golden-Headed King was about to come, and all fled and hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital had suffered repeated raids; everyone was in fear; rumor spread that the Golden-Headed King was about to come, and all fled to mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 抱貞還，而镕已迎館於鎮。

translations.literal: When Baozhen returned, Rong had already welcomed and lodged him at Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen returned, Wang Rong had already welcomed and lodged him at Zhen.

sentences.zh: 匡威引抱貞登城西大悲浮屠，顧望流涕，美其山川，乃共圖镕。

translations.literal: Kuangwei led Baozhen up the Great Compassion pagoda west of the city, looked back and wept, praised the mountains and rivers, and then together they plotted against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei led Li Baozhen up the Great Compassion pagoda west of the city, looked back and wept, praised the landscape, and together they plotted against Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 陽為镕繕甲，治城塹，施授方略，陰施予，以傾士心。

translations.literal: Outwardly he repaired armor for Rong, fortified city moats, dispensed strategy and tactics, and secretly gave favors to undermine the troops' loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he repaired armor for Rong, fortified city moats, dispensed strategy, and secretly gave favors to undermine troop loyalty.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍忠於王氏，皆惡之。

translations.literal: The Zhen army, loyal to the Wang clan, all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen army, loyal to the Wang clan, all hated him.

sentences.zh: 匡威親忌日，镕過慰。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of Kuangwei's parent's death, Rong came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Li Kuangwei's parent's death, Wang Rong came to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 匡威士衷甲劫镕入牙城，戰不勝，鎮人斬匡威以徇。

translations.literal: Kuangwei's men wore armor beneath their robes and seized Rong into the headquarters city; the battle did not succeed; the men of Zhen beheaded Kuangwei and displayed him publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei's men wore armor beneath their robes and seized Wang Rong into headquarters; the battle failed; the men of Zhen beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head publicly.

sentences.zh: 匡籌表訴諸朝，檄暴镕罪，攻樂壽、武強以報。

translations.literal: Kuangchou memorialized and appealed to the court, circulated a proclamation exposing Rong's crimes, and attacked Leshou and Wuqiang in retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou memorialized and appealed to the court, circulated a proclamation exposing Rong's crimes, and attacked Leshou and Wuqiang in retaliation.

sentences.zh: 始，匡籌之奪也，燕人不以為義。

translations.literal: At first, when Kuangchou seized power, the people of Yan did not consider it righteous.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Li Kuangchou seized power, the people of Yan did not consider it righteous.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭出奔太原，克用倚其謀，下武、媯二州，敗匡籌於居庸關。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong fled to Taiyuan; Keyong relied on his counsel, captured Wu and Gui prefectures, and defeated Kuangchou at Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong fled to Taiyuan; Li Keyong relied on his counsel, captured Wu and Gui prefectures, and defeated Li Kuangchou at Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 李存審與戰，匡籌又敗，挈其族奔京師，次景城，滄州節度使盧彥威殺之，掠入車馬僮妓。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen fought him; Kuangchou was again defeated; he fled with his clan toward the capital; halting at Jingcheng, Cangzhou military commissioner Lu Yanwei killed him and plundered his carriage, horses, servants, and entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen fought him; Li Kuangchou was again defeated; he fled with his clan toward the capital; halting at Jingcheng, Cangzhou military commissioner Lu Yanwei killed him and plundered his carriage, horses, servants, and entertainers.

sentences.zh: 妻方乳，不能進，仁恭獲之，納於克用為嬖夫人。

translations.literal: His wife was still nursing and could not proceed; Rengong captured her and presented her to Keyong as a favored consort.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was still nursing and could not proceed; Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong as a favored consort.

sentences.zh: 始，匡威見逐，嘆曰：「兄失弟得，皆吾之宗，無所悔，然其材恐不足以守。」

translations.literal: At first, when Kuangwei was driven out, he sighed and said, "Elder brother lost, younger brother gained—both are of our clan, nothing to regret; yet his talent perhaps is insufficient to hold it."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kuangwei was driven out, he sighed: "Elder brother lost, younger brother gained—both are of our clan, nothing to regret; yet his talent perhaps is insufficient to hold it."

sentences.zh: 果亡，而幽州地歸克用，以仁恭為帥。

translations.literal: Indeed he perished, and Youzhou territory returned to Keyong, who made Rengong commander.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed he perished, and Youzhou returned to Li Keyong, who made Liu Rengong commander.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭，深州人。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong was a native of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong was a native of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父晟，客范陽，為李可舉新興鎮將，故仁恭事軍中。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was a guest at Fanyang and served as garrison general of Xinxing under Li Keju; thus Rengong served in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng was a guest at Fanyang and served as garrison general of Xinxing under Li Keju; Liu Rengong thus entered military service.

sentences.zh: 從李全忠攻易州，號「窟頭」，稍遷裨校。

translations.literal: Following Li Quanzhong in the attack on Yi Prefecture, he was called "Cave Head" and was gradually promoted to deputy officer.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Quanzhong in the attack on Yi Prefecture, he was called "Cave Head" and was gradually promoted to deputy officer.

sentences.zh: 為人豪縱，多智數，有大誌，嘗自言：「夢大幡出指端，年四十九，當秉旄節。」

translations.literal: As a man he was bold and unrestrained, full of stratagems, and had great ambition; he once said himself, "I dreamed a great banner emerged from my fingertips; at age forty-nine I shall hold the staff of command."
translations.idiomatic: Bold and unrestrained, full of stratagems, and ambitious, he once said, "I dreamed a great banner emerged from my fingertips; at forty-nine I shall hold the staff of command."

sentences.zh: 李匡威惡之，補景城令。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei disliked him and appointed him magistrate of Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei disliked him and appointed him magistrate of Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 會瀛州亂，殺守吏，仁恭募士千人定其亂。

translations.literal: When Ying Prefecture fell into disorder and killed the guarding officials, Rengong recruited a thousand men and pacified the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying Prefecture rebelled and killed the guarding officials, Liu Rengong recruited a thousand men and pacified the disorder.

sentences.zh: 匡威復使將兵，戍蔚州，逾期未代，士皆怨。

translations.literal: Kuangwei again had him lead troops to garrison Wei Prefecture; when the term expired and no replacement came, the troops all resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei again had him lead troops to garrison Wei Prefecture; when the term expired with no replacement, the troops resented it.

sentences.zh: 會匡籌奪地，故戍卒擁仁恭趨幽州，匡籌逆戰，敗之，遂以族奔太原。

translations.literal: When Kuangchou seized territory, the garrison troops therefore supported Rengong and marched on Youzhou; Kuangchou met them in battle, defeated him, and Rengong then fled with his clan to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kuangchou seized territory, the garrison troops supported Liu Rengong and marched on Youzhou; Kuangchou met them in battle and defeated him; Rengong fled with his clan to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 李克用待之甚厚，賜田宅，拜壽陽鎮將。

translations.literal: Li Keyong treated him very generously, granted fields and a residence, and appointed him garrison general of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong treated him generously, granted fields and a residence, and appointed him garrison general of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 數以策幹克用，請步騎一萬東取幽州，且為導。

translations.literal: Repeatedly with stratagems he approached Keyong, requesting ten thousand infantry and cavalry to take Youzhou in the east and serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he approached Li Keyong with stratagems, requesting ten thousand infantry and cavalry to take Youzhou in the east and serve as guide.

sentences.zh: 克用攻匡籌，匡籌遁去。

translations.literal: Keyong attacked Kuangchou, and Kuangchou fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong attacked Li Kuangchou, and Kuangchou fled.

sentences.zh: 仁恭與苻存審入城，封府庫以待。

translations.literal: Rengong together with Fu Cunshen entered the city, sealed the treasury and storehouses, and awaited him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong together with Fu Cunshen entered the city, sealed the treasury and storehouses, and awaited Keyong.

sentences.zh: 克用悅，留仁恭守之，以親信分典其兵。

translations.literal: Keyong was pleased, left Rengong to guard it, and had trusted men share command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was pleased, left Liu Rengong to guard it, and had trusted men share command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，克用擊王行瑜，表仁恭為檢校司空、盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Keyong attacked Wang Xingyu and memorialized to make Rengong acting minister of works and military commissioner of the Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 895, Li Keyong attacked Wang Xingyu and memorialized to appoint Liu Rengong acting minister of works and military commissioner of the Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，克用攻魏州，召盧龍兵，仁恭以契丹解。

translations.literal: The next year Keyong attacked Wei Prefecture and summoned Lulong troops; Rengong excused himself citing the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Keyong attacked Wei Prefecture and summoned Lulong troops; Liu Rengong excused himself citing the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又明年，克用復興其兵救朱瑄，仁恭不答，使者數十往，卒不出。

translations.literal: The year after that, Keyong again raised his troops to rescue Zhu Xuan; Rengong did not respond; dozens of envoys went back and forth, yet in the end he did not dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Li Keyong again raised troops to rescue Zhu Xuan; Liu Rengong did not respond; dozens of envoys went back and forth, yet he never dispatched troops.

sentences.zh: 克用以書讓之，仁恭乃慢罵，執其使，盡囚太原士之在燕者。

translations.literal: Keyong reproached him by letter; Rengong then insulted and reviled him, seized his envoys, and imprisoned all Taiyuan men who were in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong reproached him by letter; Liu Rengong insulted and reviled him, seized his envoys, and imprisoned all Taiyuan men in Yan.

sentences.zh: 復以厚利誘克用麾下士，多亡歸之。

translations.literal: He again used rich rewards to entice Keyong's subordinates, and many fled back to him.
translations.idiomatic: He again used rich rewards to entice Li Keyong's subordinates, and many defected to him.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，自將往擊，不勝，師喪過半。

translations.literal: Keyong was angry and personally led troops to attack; he did not succeed, and more than half the army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was furious and personally led troops to attack; he failed, and more than half the army was lost.

sentences.zh: 仁恭獻馘於朱全忠，全忠表同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Rengong presented severed heads to Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong memorialized to make him co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong presented severed heads to Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong memorialized to make him co-director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既與克用絕，則益募兵。

translations.literal: Having broken with Keyong, he then increased recruitment of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Having broken with Li Keyong, he increased recruitment of troops.

sentences.zh: 光化初，使其子守文襲滄州，節度使盧彥威棄城走，遂有滄、景、德三州地，用守文為節度留後，請命於朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua he had his son Shouwen raid Cang Prefecture; military commissioner Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled; he then held the territories of Cang, Jing, and De prefectures, used Shouwen as acting military commissioner, and requested appointment from the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guanghua era he had his son Shouwen raid Cang Prefecture; military commissioner Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled; he then held Cang, Jing, and De prefectures, installed Shouwen as acting commissioner, and requested appointment from the court.

sentences.zh: 昭宗怒，不與。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was angry and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong was angry and refused.

sentences.zh: 會中人至，仁恭謾謂曰：「旄節吾自可為，要假長安本色耳，何見拒邪？」

translations.literal: When an eunuch arrived, Rengong insolently said to him, "The staff of command I can make myself—I only need to borrow the proper Chang'an style; why be refused?"
translations.idiomatic: When an eunuch arrived, Liu Rengong insolently said, "The staff of command I can make myself—I only need to borrow the proper Chang'an style; why be refused?"

sentences.zh: 由是兵益張，顯圖河北。

translations.literal: Thereupon his troops grew ever bolder and he openly plotted for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his troops grew bolder and he openly plotted for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 悉幽、滄步騎十萬，聲言三十萬，南徇魏、鎮。

translations.literal: He mustered a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from You and Cang, claiming three hundred thousand, and marched south against Wei and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from You and Cang, claiming three hundred thousand, and marched south against Wei and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 次貝州，屠之，清水為不流。

translations.literal: He halted at Bei Prefecture and massacred it; the clear water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Bei Prefecture and massacred it; the clear water ran red and ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威求救於朱全忠，全忠使李思安、葛從周赴之，屯內黃。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei sought rescue from Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong sent Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou to go to his aid and encamped at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei sought rescue from Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong sent Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou to his aid, encamping at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 仁恭負強，下令曰：「思安懦，當先破之，乃取魏。」

translations.literal: Rengong, relying on his strength, issued an order, saying, "Si'an is cowardly—we should first break him, then take Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his strength, Liu Rengong ordered, "Si'an is cowardly—we should break him first, then take Wei."

sentences.zh: 守文與單可及精甲五萬，循清水上。

translations.literal: Shouwen together with Shan Keji with fifty thousand elite armored troops advanced along the clear water upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen and Shan Keji with fifty thousand elite armored troops advanced along the clear water upstream.

sentences.zh: 思安設伏，自引兵逆戰，偽不勝。

translations.literal: Si'an set an ambush, personally led troops to meet the attack, and feigned defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an set an ambush, personally led troops to meet the attack, and feigned defeat.

sentences.zh: 守文躡北至內黃，思安整兵還擊守文，伏發，斬可及，獨守文挺逸，眾無還者。

translations.literal: Shouwen pursued north to Neihuang; Si'an reformed his troops and counterattacked Shouwen; the ambush sprang forth; Keji was beheaded; only Shouwen escaped by force; none of the troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen pursued north to Neihuang; Li Si'an reformed his troops and counterattacked; the ambush sprang forth; Keji was beheaded; only Shouwen escaped; none of his troops returned.

sentences.zh: 從周興邢、洺兵與魏將賀德倫等出館陶門，夜擊仁恭，破八屯。

translations.literal: Congzhou raised Xing and Ming troops together with Wei generals He Delun and others, went out through Guantao Gate, attacked Rengong by night, and broke eight encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou raised Xing and Ming troops together with Wei generals He Delun and others, sallied through Guantao Gate, attacked Liu Rengong by night, and broke eight encampments.

sentences.zh: 仁恭走，自魏抵長河數百里，屍蔽道。

translations.literal: Rengong fled; from Wei to Changhe for several hundred li, corpses covered the road.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong fled; from Wei to Changhe for several hundred li, corpses covered the road.

sentences.zh: 鎮人邀敗之東境。

translations.literal: The men of Zhen intercepted and defeated him on the eastern border.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Zhen intercepted and defeated him on the eastern border.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遂衰。

translations.literal: Rengong then declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong then declined.

sentences.zh: 三年，葛從周攻滄州，仁恭壁乾寧。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ge Congzhou attacked Cang Prefecture; Rengong fortified at Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Ge Congzhou attacked Cang Prefecture; Liu Rengong fortified at Qianning.

sentences.zh: 從周潛軍戰老鴉堤，仁恭敗，退壁瓦橋，卑辭歸窮於克用求救，克用為侵邢、洺。

translations.literal: Congzhou secretly deployed troops and fought at Laoya Embankment; Rengong was defeated, retreated to fortify at Waqiao, with humble words returned in desperation to Keyong seeking rescue; Keyong raided Xing and Ming for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou secretly deployed troops and fought at Laoya Embankment; Liu Rengong was defeated, retreated to fortify at Waqiao, and in desperation returned to Li Keyong seeking rescue; Keyong raided Xing and Ming on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 俄而全忠取瀛、莫，克用使周德威出飛狐。

translations.literal: Before long Quanzhong took Ying and Mo; Keyong had Zhou Dewei go out through Feihu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Quanzhong took Ying and Mo; Li Keyong had Zhou Dewei go out through Feihu Pass.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，全忠自將攻滄州，壁長蘆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Quanzhong personally led troops to attack Cang Prefecture and encamped at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: In 906, Zhu Quanzhong personally led troops to attack Cang Prefecture and encamped at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 仁恭悉發男子十五以上為兵，涅其面曰「定霸都」，士人則涅於臂曰：「一心事主」，盧龍閭裏為空，得眾二十萬，屯瓦橋。

translations.literal: Rengong mustered all males fifteen and above as soldiers, tattooed their faces with "Dingba Capital," and for scholars tattooed their arms with "Wholeheartedly serving the lord"; Lulong's villages and lanes were emptied; he gathered two hundred thousand troops and encamped at Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong mustered all males fifteen and above as soldiers, tattooed their faces with "Dingba Capital," and for scholars tattooed their arms with "Wholeheartedly serving the lord"; Lulong's villages were emptied; he gathered two hundred thousand troops and encamped at Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 全忠環滄築而溝之，內外援絕，人相食。

translations.literal: Quanzhong surrounded Cang, built fortifications and dug moats; internal and external aid was cut off, and people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong surrounded Cang, built fortifications and dug moats; aid was cut off inside and out, and people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 仁恭求戰，不許，復從克用乞師，使百輩往，乃許。

translations.literal: Rengong requested battle but was not permitted; he again begged Keyong for troops, sent a hundred envoys, and only then was granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong requested battle but was refused; he again begged Li Keyong for troops, sent a hundred envoys, and only then was granted permission.

sentences.zh: 仁恭以兵三萬合攻潞州，降全忠將丁會，滄州圍乃解。

translations.literal: Rengong with thirty thousand troops jointly attacked Lu Prefecture, induced Quanzhong's general Ding Hui to surrender, and the siege of Cang Prefecture was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong with thirty thousand troops jointly attacked Lu Prefecture, induced Zhu Quanzhong's general Ding Hui to surrender, and the siege of Cang was lifted.

sentences.zh: 是時，中原方多故，仁恭得倚燕強且遠，無所憚，意自滿。

translations.literal: At that time the central plains were in great turmoil; Rengong could rely on Yan being strong and remote, feared nothing, and was self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the central plains were in turmoil; Liu Rengong, relying on Yan's strength and remoteness, feared nothing and grew complacent.

sentences.zh: 從方士王若訥學長年，築館大安山，掠子女充之。

translations.literal: He studied longevity from the adept Wang Ruone, built a lodge on Mount Da'an, and plundered women and children to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: He studied longevity from the adept Wang Ruone, built a lodge on Mount Da'an, and plundered women and children to fill it.

sentences.zh: 又招浮屠，與講法。

translations.literal: He also recruited Buddhist monks and expounded the dharma with them.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited Buddhist monks and expounded the dharma with them.

sentences.zh: 以堇土為錢，斂真錢，穴山藏之，殺匠滅口。

translations.literal: He used clay for coinage, collected real money, hid it in mountain caves, and killed the craftsmen to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: He minted coins from clay, collected real money, hid it in mountain caves, and killed the craftsmen to silence them.

sentences.zh: 禁南方茶，自擷山為茶，號山曰大恩，以邀利。

translations.literal: He banned southern tea, gathered mountain tea himself, named the mountain Da'en, and sought profit.
translations.idiomatic: He banned southern tea, gathered mountain tea himself, named the mountain Da'en, and monopolized the profit.

sentences.zh: 子守光烝嬖妾，事覺，仁恭謫之。

translations.literal: His son Shouguang violated a favored concubine; when the matter was discovered, Rengong banished him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouguang violated a favored concubine; when the matter was discovered, Liu Rengong banished him.

sentences.zh: 李思安來攻，屯石子河。

translations.literal: Li Si'an came to attack and encamped at Shizi River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an came to attack and encamped at Shizi River.

sentences.zh: 仁恭居大安山，城中無備。

translations.literal: Rengong dwelt on Mount Da'an; the city had no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong dwelt on Mount Da'an; the city had no defenses.

sentences.zh: 守光引兵出戰，思安去，因回攻大安，虜仁恭，囚別室，殺左右婢媵，遂有盧龍。

translations.literal: Shouguang led troops out to fight; Si'an departed; Shouguang then turned back to attack Da'an, captured Rengong, imprisoned him in a separate chamber, killed the attendants and concubines at his side, and then held Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang led troops out to fight; Si'an departed; Shouguang then turned back to attack Da'an, captured Liu Rengong, imprisoned him in a separate chamber, killed his attendants and concubines, and seized Lulong.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：朱滔脅其兄泚入朝，及引兵東向，稱帝以自尊，名雖助泚，誌可知矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zhu Tao coerced his elder brother Ci to enter court, and when he led troops eastward and proclaimed himself emperor to elevate himself, though in name he aided Ci, his intent was clear.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Zhu Tao coerced his elder brother Ci to enter court, and when he led troops eastward and proclaimed himself emperor to elevate himself, though in name he aided Ci, his intent was clear.

sentences.zh: 至克融再得幽州，朱氏無遺種，其禍與泚鈞，而族夷有先後為間也。

translations.literal: When Kerong again obtained Youzhou, the Zhu clan left no survivors; their calamity equaled Ci's, yet the extermination of the clan had intervals of precedence and delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Kerong again obtained Youzhou, the Zhu clan left no survivors; their calamity equaled Ci's, yet the extermination of the clan came with intervals between the first and the last.
